title.hinglish: Abhimanyu: garbh mein sunne wala baalak

text.en: Long ago, in the kingdom of the Pandavas, Princess Subhadra was expecting a baby. Every evening her husband, the great archer Arjuna, sat beside her. He told her stories of the forests, the rivers and the stars. Subhadra would rest her hands on her belly and smile, because she felt the baby was listening too.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle, Pandavon ke raajya mein, Rajkumari Subhadra maa banne wali thi. Har shaam unke pati, mahaan dhanurdhar Arjun, unke paas baithte. Woh jungle, nadiyon aur taaron ki kahaniyan sunaate. Subhadra pet par haath rakh kar muskuraati, kyonki unhe lagta tha ki baby bhi sun raha hai.
text.hi: बहुत पहले, पांडवों के राज्य में, राजकुमारी सुभद्रा माँ बनने वाली थीं। हर शाम उनके पति, महान धनुर्धर अर्जुन, उनके पास बैठते। वह जंगल, नदियों और तारों की कहानियाँ सुनाते। सुभद्रा पेट पर हाथ रखकर मुस्कुरातीं, क्योंकि उन्हें लगता था कि बच्चा भी सुन रहा है।

text.en: One night Subhadra asked, 'Tell me about the chakravyuh, the puzzle-shaped army that no one can enter.' Arjuna drew circles in the air. 'It is like a spinning lotus,' he said. 'Ring inside ring. To enter, you must find the gap at the right moment and move without fear.'
text.hinglish: Ek raat Subhadra ne poochha, 'Mujhe chakravyuh ke baare mein bataiye, woh paheli jaisi sena jisme koi ghus nahi sakta.' Arjun ne hawa mein gol ghere banaaye. 'Yeh ghoomte kamal jaisa hai,' unhone kaha. 'Ghere ke andar ghera. Andar jaane ke liye sahi pal par raasta dhoondhna hota hai aur bina dare aage badhna hota hai.'
text.hi: एक रात सुभद्रा ने पूछा, 'मुझे चक्रव्यूह के बारे में बताइए, वह पहेली जैसी सेना जिसमें कोई घुस नहीं सकता।' अर्जुन ने हवा में गोल घेरे बनाए। 'यह घूमते कमल जैसा है,' उन्होंने कहा। 'घेरे के अंदर घेरा। अंदर जाने के लिए सही पल पर रास्ता ढूँढना होता है और बिना डरे आगे बढ़ना होता है।'

text.en: Arjuna explained the first ring, then the second, then the third. Inside Subhadra, the baby was very still, as if paying close attention. But the night was warm and Arjuna's voice was soft. Before he could explain how to come back out, Subhadra had gently fallen asleep.
text.hinglish: Arjun ne pehla ghera samjhaaya, phir doosra, phir teesra. Subhadra ke andar baby bilkul shaant tha, jaise dhyaan se sun raha ho. Par raat garm thi aur Arjun ki awaaz narm. Bahar nikalne ka tareeka bataane se pehle hi Subhadra ko pyaari si neend aa gayi.
text.hi: अर्जुन ने पहला घेरा समझाया, फिर दूसरा, फिर तीसरा। सुभद्रा के अंदर बच्चा बिल्कुल शांत था, जैसे ध्यान से सुन रहा हो। पर रात गर्म थी और अर्जुन की आवाज़ नरम। बाहर निकलने का तरीका बताने से पहले ही सुभद्रा को प्यारी सी नींद आ गई।

text.en: The baby was born and named Abhimanyu, which means 'brave and full of spirit'. He grew up to be a fine young archer. And here is the wonder: he already knew how to enter the chakravyuh. He had learned it while still in his mother's womb, listening to his parents talk.
text.hinglish: Baby ka janm hua aur naam rakha gaya Abhimanyu, yaani 'bahadur aur josh se bhara'. Woh bada hokar ek kushal dhanurdhar bana. Aur kamaal ki baat: use chakravyuh mein ghusna pehle se aata tha. Usne yeh maa ke garbh mein, maata-pita ki baatein sunte hue seekha tha.
text.hi: बच्चे का जन्म हुआ और नाम रखा गया अभिमन्यु, यानी 'बहादुर और जोश से भरा'। वह बड़ा होकर एक कुशल धनुर्धर बना। और कमाल की बात: उसे चक्रव्यूह में घुसना पहले से आता था। उसने यह माँ के गर्भ में, माता-पिता की बातें सुनते हुए सीखा था।

text.en: Years later, on the field of Kurukshetra, here in our own Haryana, the Pandavas faced the chakravyuh. Arjuna was far away. Only young Abhimanyu knew how to break in. Everyone turned to him.
text.hinglish: Saalon baad, Kurukshetra ke maidaan mein, hamare apne Haryana mein, Pandavon ke saamne chakravyuh tha. Arjun door the. Sirf yuva Abhimanyu ko andar ghusna aata tha. Sab ne uski taraf dekha.
text.hi: सालों बाद, कुरुक्षेत्र के मैदान में, हमारे अपने हरियाणा में, पांडवों के सामने चक्रव्यूह था। अर्जुन दूर थे। सिर्फ़ युवा अभिमन्यु को अंदर घुसना आता था। सबने उसकी तरफ़ देखा।

label.en: Go in bravely to help his family
label.hinglish: Parivaar ki madad ke liye himmat se andar jaaye

lesson.en: Abhimanyu did go in, like a lion. Courage means doing the right thing even when your heart beats fast.
lesson.hinglish: Abhimanyu sher ki tarah andar gaya. Himmat ka matlab hai dil tez dhadke tab bhi sahi kaam karna.

label.en: Ask the elders to come in with him
label.hinglish: Bado se kahe ki saath andar chalein

lesson.en: That was exactly the plan! Abhimanyu would open the way and his uncles would follow. Asking for help is wisdom, not weakness.
lesson.hinglish: Yahi to yojana thi! Abhimanyu raasta kholta aur chacha log peeche aate. Madad maangna samajhdaari hai, kamzori nahi.

text.en: Abhimanyu broke through ring after ring, brave as a lion. Poets in Haryana and all over India still sing of his courage. And mothers still remember the most beautiful part of his story: a baby can hear, and love, and learn, even before being born.
text.hinglish: Abhimanyu sher ki tarah ek ke baad ek ghera todta gaya. Haryana aur poore Bharat ke kavi aaj bhi uski himmat ke geet gaate hain. Aur maayein uski kahani ka sabse sundar hissa yaad rakhti hain: baby janm se pehle bhi sun sakta hai, pyaar kar sakta hai, seekh sakta hai.
text.hi: अभिमन्यु शेर की तरह एक के बाद एक घेरा तोड़ता गया। हरियाणा और पूरे भारत के कवि आज भी उसकी हिम्मत के गीत गाते हैं। और माताएँ उसकी कहानी का सबसे सुंदर हिस्सा याद रखती हैं: बच्चा जन्म से पहले भी सुन सकता है, प्यार कर सकता है, सीख सकता है।

say.en: Little one, I know you are listening. I love you, and I will tell you all the stories, right to the end.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, mujhe pata hai tum sun rahe ho. Mujhe tumse pyaar hai, aur main tumhe har kahani poori sunaaungi.

moral.en: Babies feel our voices and our love. And when we learn something, it's good to learn it all the way to the end.
moral.hinglish: Baby hamari awaaz aur pyaar mehsoos karta hai. Aur jab kuch seekhein, to poora seekhna achha hai.

reflection.en: What is one thing you would love your baby to hear from you every day?
reflection.hinglish: Aap roz baby ko apni taraf se kya sunaana chahengi?

q.en: Abhimanyu learned about the chakravyuh before he was born.
q.hinglish: Abhimanyu ne chakravyuh ke baare mein janm se pehle seekha.

q.en: Subhadra heard the whole explanation, including how to come out.
q.hinglish: Subhadra ne bahar nikalne ka tareeka bhi poora suna.

q.en: Kurukshetra is in Haryana.
q.hinglish: Kurukshetra Haryana mein hai.

q.en: Abhimanyu's name means 'sleepy and slow'.
q.hinglish: Abhimanyu naam ka matlab hai 'neend bhara aur dheema'.

title.hinglish: Gita Week, Bhaag 1: Arjun ki uljhan

text.en: At Kurukshetra, two great armies stood facing each other. Conches blew, horses stamped, and flags waved in the wind. In a shining chariot sat Arjuna, the finest archer of his time. Holding the reins was his dear friend and guide, Krishna.
text.hinglish: Kurukshetra mein do badi senaayein aamne-saamne khadi thi. Shankh baje, ghode hinhinaaye, aur jhande hawa mein lehraaye. Ek chamakte rath mein Arjun baithe the, apne samay ke sabse achhe dhanurdhar. Lagaam unke pyaare dost aur maargdarshak Krishna ke haath mein thi.

text.en: 'Krishna,' said Arjuna, 'take my chariot to the middle. I want to see who stands before me.' Krishna smiled and drove forward. Arjuna looked across, and his heart sank. On the other side were his teachers, his cousins, his elders, people he loved.
text.hinglish: 'Krishna,' Arjun bole, 'mera rath beech mein le chaliye. Main dekhna chahta hoon saamne kaun khada hai.' Krishna muskuraaye aur rath aage badhaaya. Arjun ne dekha aur unka dil baith gaya. Doosri taraf unke guru, chachere bhai, buzurg the, jinse woh pyaar karte the.

text.en: His hands began to shake. His great bow, Gandiva, slipped from his fingers. 'I can't do this,' he whispered. 'My mouth is dry, my mind is spinning. I don't know what is right any more.' The mighty Arjuna sat down in the chariot, full of worry.
text.hinglish: Unke haath kaanpne lage. Unka mahaan dhanush, Gandiv, haathon se phisal gaya. 'Mujhse nahi hoga,' woh dheere se bole. 'Mera munh sookh raha hai, mann ghoom raha hai. Mujhe ab samajh nahi aata kya sahi hai.' Mahaan Arjun chintit hokar rath mein baith gaye.

text.en: Krishna did not scold him. He did not laugh. He sat beside his friend and listened. Sometimes, the bravest person in the world also feels afraid. Feeling worried does not make us weak. It means we care deeply.
text.hinglish: Krishna ne unhe daanta nahi. Hanse bhi nahi. Woh dost ke paas baithe aur suna. Kabhi-kabhi duniya ka sabse bahadur insaan bhi darta hai. Chinta hona hume kamzor nahi banata. Iska matlab hai hum gehraai se parwaah karte hain.

text.en: Then Krishna spoke gently: 'Arjuna, cold and heat, happiness and sadness, they come and they go, like seasons. They do not stay. Be patient with them.' This is the shloka of today: maatra-sparshas tu kaunteya... Feelings are like clouds passing over the sun.
text.hinglish: Phir Krishna ne pyaar se kaha: 'Arjun, sardi aur garmi, sukh aur dukh, mausam ki tarah aate hain aur chale jaate hain. Yeh tikte nahi. Inhe dheeraj se saho.' Yahi aaj ka shloka hai: maatra-sparshas tu kaunteya... Bhaavnaayein suraj ke aage se guzarte baadalon jaisi hain.

say.en: Little one, whatever you feel, I am here. Feelings pass like clouds, and my love stays like the sun.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum jo bhi mehsoos karo, main yahan hoon. Bhaav baadal ki tarah guzar jaate hain, aur mera pyaar suraj ki tarah rehta hai.

text.en: Arjuna took a long, slow breath. He was still unsure, but he was listening now. He looked at Krishna and said, 'Teach me. Help me understand.' And Krishna began to speak the words that we now call the Bhagavad Gita. Part 2 tomorrow ✨
text.hinglish: Arjun ne ek lambi, dheemi saans li. Woh abhi bhi uljhan mein the, par ab sun rahe the. Unhone Krishna se kaha, 'Mujhe sikhaaiye. Samajhne mein madad kijiye.' Aur Krishna ne woh shabd kehne shuru kiye jinhe hum aaj Bhagavad Gita kehte hain. Bhaag 2 kal ✨

moral.en: Even brave people feel worried sometimes. Feelings come and go. Breathe, and ask for help.
moral.hinglish: Bahadur log bhi kabhi-kabhi chintit hote hain. Bhaav aate-jaate hain. Saans lijiye aur madad maangiye.

reflection.en: What helps you when you feel worried?
reflection.hinglish: Jab aap chintit hoti hain, to kya madad karta hai?

q.en: Krishna was driving Arjuna's chariot.
q.hinglish: Krishna Arjun ka rath chala rahe the.

q.en: Krishna scolded Arjuna for feeling afraid.
q.hinglish: Krishna ne darne ke liye Arjun ko daanta.

q.en: The shloka says feelings come and go like seasons.
q.hinglish: Shloka kehta hai ki bhaav mausam ki tarah aate-jaate hain.

title.en: Gita Week, Part 2: Krishna's calm advice
title.hinglish: Gita Week, Bhaag 2: Krishna ki shaant seekh

text.en: Yesterday, Arjuna sat down in his chariot, worried and unsure. Today, Krishna continued speaking. His voice was calm, like water in a deep river. Around them the armies waited, but inside the chariot it felt peaceful.
text.hinglish: Kal Arjun chintit hokar rath mein baith gaye the. Aaj Krishna ne baat aage badhaayi. Unki awaaz gehri nadi ke paani jaisi shaant thi. Chaaron taraf senaayein intezaar kar rahi thi, par rath ke andar sukoon tha.

text.en: 'Arjuna,' said Krishna, 'think of a farmer in Haryana. He ploughs the field, sows the wheat, waters it, and protects it from birds. He does everything he can. But can he order the rain to come?' Arjuna shook his head. 'No. The rain comes when it comes.'
text.hinglish: 'Arjun,' Krishna bole, 'Haryana ke ek kisaan ke baare mein socho. Woh khet jotta hai, gehun boota hai, paani deta hai, chidiyon se bachaata hai. Jo kar sakta hai, sab karta hai. Par kya woh baarish ko hukm de sakta hai?' Arjun ne sir hilaaya. 'Nahi. Baarish apne samay par aati hai.'

text.en: 'Exactly,' said Krishna. 'So the wise farmer does his work with love and care, and then he stays calm. If the harvest is big, he is thankful. If it is small, he does not lose heart. He keeps going.'
text.hinglish: 'Bilkul,' Krishna bole. 'Isliye samajhdaar kisaan pyaar aur dhyaan se apna kaam karta hai, aur phir shaant rehta hai. Fasal achhi ho to shukriya kehta hai. Kam ho to himmat nahi haarta. Woh chalta rehta hai.'

text.en: 'Yogasthah kuru karmani,' said Krishna. 'Stay steady and do your work. Be the same in success and in failure. This even, balanced mind is called yoga.' Yoga is not only stretching. It is a calm heart that stays kind on good days and hard days.
text.hinglish: 'Yogasthah kuru karmani,' Krishna ne kaha. 'Sthir rehkar apna kaam karo. Safalta aur asafalta mein ek jaise raho. Is santulit mann ko yog kehte hain.' Yog sirf aasan nahi hai. Yeh woh shaant dil hai jo achhe aur kathin, dono dino mein komal rehta hai.

text.en: Arjuna thought about this. 'So I should not worry about everything that might happen?' 'Do your part with your whole heart,' said Krishna, 'and let the rest unfold.' Arjuna felt his shoulders soften. His breathing became slow and deep.
text.hinglish: Arjun ne socha. 'To mujhe har hone wali baat ki chinta nahi karni chahiye?' 'Apna hissa poore mann se karo,' Krishna bole, 'aur baaki ko hone do.' Arjun ke kandhe dheele ho gaye. Unki saans dheemi aur gehri ho gayi.

say.en: Little one, we will do our best each day, and we will stay calm together.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, hum roz apna best karenge, aur saath mein shaant rahenge.

text.en: Just like Arjuna, a mother-to-be does so much: eating well, resting, taking her tablets, loving her baby. She can do her part with love, and let the rest unfold with trust. Part 3 tomorrow ✨
text.hinglish: Arjun ki tarah, maa banne wali bhi bahut kuch karti hai: achha khaana, aaraam, tablet, aur baby se pyaar. Woh pyaar se apna hissa kar sakti hai, aur baaki bharose ke saath hone de sakti hai. Bhaag 3 kal ✨

moral.en: Do your part with love, and keep a calm, balanced heart, whatever happens.
moral.hinglish: Pyaar se apna hissa karo, aur jo bhi ho, mann shaant aur santulit rakho.

reflection.en: What is one thing you are doing with love for your baby this week?
reflection.hinglish: Is hafte aap baby ke liye pyaar se kaun sa kaam kar rahi hain?

q.en: Krishna compared Arjuna's work to a farmer's work.
q.hinglish: Krishna ne Arjun ke kaam ki tulna kisaan se ki.

q.en: The farmer can order the rain to come.
q.hinglish: Kisaan baarish ko hukm de sakta hai.

q.en: Yoga, in this shloka, means a calm, balanced mind.
q.hinglish: Is shloke mein yog ka matlab hai shaant, santulit mann.

title.en: Gita Week, Part 3: Do your best and let go
title.hinglish: Gita Week, Bhaag 3: Apna best karo, phal chhodo

text.en: On the third day of our Gita Week, Arjuna had one more question. 'Krishna, if I can't control what happens, why should I try at all?' It was an honest question, and Krishna loved honest questions.
text.hinglish: Gita Week ke teesre din, Arjun ka ek aur sawaal tha. 'Krishna, agar jo hota hai woh mere haath mein nahi, to koshish hi kyon karoon?' Yeh sachcha sawaal tha, aur Krishna ko sachche sawaal bahut pasand the.

text.en: Krishna answered with the most famous lines of the Gita: 'Karmanye vadhikaraste, ma phaleshu kadachana.' Your right is to the doing, never to the fruits. 'But,' he added, 'never let that make you stop doing. Don't sit idle either.'
text.hinglish: Krishna ne Gita ki sabse prasiddh panktiyon se jawaab diya: 'Karmanye vadhikaraste, ma phaleshu kadachana.' Tumhara haq karm par hai, phal par kabhi nahi. 'Par,' unhone joda, 'iska matlab yeh nahi ki kaam chhod do. Khaali bhi mat baitho.'

text.en: He pointed to a little sparrow building a nest. 'Look. She carries one straw at a time. She does not know if the wind will blow. But she builds with all her heart, every single day. That is how we should live: busy with love, free from worry.'
text.hinglish: Unhone ghonsla banaati ek nanhi chidiya ki taraf ishaara kiya. 'Dekho. Woh ek baar mein ek tinka laati hai. Use nahi pata hawa chalegi ya nahi. Par woh roz poore dil se banaati hai. Hume bhi aise hi jeena chahiye: pyaar mein vyast, chinta se mukt.'

question.en: A storm knocks down part of the sparrow's nest. What should she do?
question.hinglish: Toofan chidiya ke ghonsle ka hissa gira deta hai. Use kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Rest a little, then build again
label.hinglish: Thoda aaraam, phir se banaaye

lesson.en: Yes! Resting is part of doing your best. Then she begins again, one straw at a time.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Aaraam bhi best karne ka hissa hai. Phir woh ek-ek tinke se dobaara shuru karti hai.

label.en: Ask her friends to help
label.hinglish: Saheliyon se madad maange

lesson.en: Lovely! Many birds working together build faster. Doing your best includes letting others help you.
lesson.hinglish: Bahut badhiya! Kai chidiyan milkar jaldi banaati hain. Best karne mein doosron ki madad lena bhi shaamil hai.

text.en: Arjuna understood. He did not need to carry the whole world on his shoulders. He only needed to do his own part, honestly and bravely, and trust the rest. He picked up his bow, and his hands were steady now.
text.hinglish: Arjun samajh gaye. Unhe poori duniya ka bojh kandhe par nahi uthaana tha. Bas apna hissa imaandaari aur himmat se karna tha, aur baaki par bharosa. Unhone dhanush uthaaya, aur ab unke haath sthir the.

text.en: These words were spoken at Kurukshetra, in Haryana, thousands of years ago. Every year, people from all over the world come to the Gita Mahotsav there. And today, these same words have reached you and your baby.
text.hinglish: Yeh shabd hazaaron saal pehle Haryana ke Kurukshetra mein kahe gaye the. Har saal duniya bhar se log wahan Gita Mahotsav mein aate hain. Aur aaj, yahi shabd aap tak aur aapke baby tak pahunche hain.

say.en: Little one, do your best, stay kind, and let go of worry. Mummy is learning this too.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, apna best karna, komal rehna, aur chinta chhod dena. Mummy bhi yeh seekh rahi hai.

text.en: Gita Week is complete! 🌸 Over three days you have heard Arjuna's doubt, Krishna's calm advice, and the secret of doing your best and letting go. You can replay any part from your story library whenever you like.
text.hinglish: Gita Week poora hua! 🌸 Teen din mein aapne Arjun ki uljhan, Krishna ki shaant seekh, aur best karke phal chhodne ka raaz suna. Kabhi bhi apni kahani library se koi bhi bhaag dobaara sun sakti hain.

moral.en: Do your best with love, rest when you need to, and let go of what you can't control.
moral.hinglish: Pyaar se apna best karo, zaroorat ho to aaraam karo, aur jo haath mein nahi use chhod do.

reflection.en: What is one worry you would like to let go of today?
reflection.hinglish: Aaj aap kaun si ek chinta chhodna chahengi?

q.en: Krishna said we have a right only to our actions, not their results.
q.hinglish: Krishna ne kaha hamara haq sirf karm par hai, phal par nahi.

q.en: Krishna said that means we should stop working.
q.hinglish: Krishna ne kaha iska matlab hai kaam band kar do.

q.en: The sparrow built her nest one straw at a time.
q.hinglish: Chidiya ne ek-ek tinke se ghonsla banaaya.

q.en: The Gita Mahotsav is held in Kurukshetra.
q.hinglish: Gita Mahotsav Kurukshetra mein hota hai.

text.en: King Uttanapada had two sons. Little Dhruva was the son of Queen Suniti, and Uttama was the son of Queen Suruchi. One day five-year-old Dhruva saw his brother sitting on their father's lap. He ran to climb up too, his arms stretched wide.
text.hinglish: Raja Uttanpaad ke do bete the. Nanha Dhruv Rani Suniti ka beta tha, aur Uttam Rani Suruchi ka. Ek din paanch saal ke Dhruv ne bhai ko pita ki god mein baithe dekha. Woh bhi baahein phailaakar god mein chadhne bhaaga.

text.en: But Queen Suruchi stopped him. 'You cannot sit there,' she said sharply. The king stayed quiet. Dhruva's eyes filled with tears, and he ran to his mother. 'Maa, why can't I sit with Pitaji?'
text.hinglish: Par Rani Suruchi ne use rok diya. 'Tum yahan nahi baith sakte,' unhone sakhti se kaha. Raja chup rahe. Dhruv ki aankhein bhar aayi, aur woh maa ke paas bhaaga. 'Maa, main Pitaji ke paas kyon nahi baith sakta?'

text.en: Queen Suniti held him close. She did not say an angry word about anyone. 'My son,' she said softly, 'don't keep anger in your heart. Pray to Lord Vishnu. His lap has room for everyone.'
text.hinglish: Rani Suniti ne use gale lagaaya. Unhone kisi ke baare mein ek bhi gussa bhara shabd nahi kaha. 'Beta,' woh dheere se boli, 'dil mein gussa mat rakho. Bhagwan Vishnu se prarthana karo. Unki god mein sabke liye jagah hai.'

say.en: Little one, there will always be room for you in my arms.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, meri baahon mein tumhare liye hamesha jagah rahegi.

text.en: Dhruva went to the forest and sat to pray. The sage Narada came to test him. 'You are so small,' said Narada. 'Go home. This is too hard for you.' But Dhruva smiled. 'I have decided. I will keep trying.'
text.hinglish: Dhruv jungle gaya aur prarthana mein baith gaya. Narad Muni use parakhne aaye. 'Tum bahut chhote ho,' Narad bole. 'Ghar jao. Yeh tumhare liye bahut kathin hai.' Par Dhruv muskuraaya. 'Maine tay kar liya hai. Main koshish karta rahoonga.'

question.en: What should little Dhruva do when Narada says it is too hard?
question.hinglish: Jab Narad kehte hain yeh bahut kathin hai, to nanhe Dhruv ko kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Keep trying, step by step
label.hinglish: Kadam-dar-kadam koshish karta rahe

lesson.en: That's what Dhruva did! Narada was so pleased that he taught him a mantra to help him.
lesson.hinglish: Dhruv ne yahi kiya! Narad itne khush hue ki unhone use madad ke liye ek mantra sikhaaya.

label.en: Ask Narada to guide him
label.hinglish: Narad se maargdarshan maange

lesson.en: Wise! Narada happily taught him the mantra 'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya'. A good teacher makes hard things easier.
lesson.hinglish: Samajhdaari! Narad ne khushi se use 'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya' mantra sikhaaya. Achha guru kathin cheez aasaan bana deta hai.

text.en: Dhruva prayed with so much focus that the whole sky seemed to hold its breath. Season after season, he stayed steady. At last Lord Vishnu appeared and touched his cheek with love. 'Dhruva, your determination is beautiful.'
text.hinglish: Dhruv ne itne dhyaan se prarthana ki ki poora aasmaan jaise saans roke dekh raha tha. Mausam badalte rahe, par woh atal raha. Aakhir Bhagwan Vishnu prakat hue aur pyaar se uske gaal ko chhua. 'Dhruv, tumhara sankalp bahut sundar hai.'

text.en: Dhruva came home, and his father welcomed him with open arms. When he grew up, he became a kind and fair king. And Lord Vishnu gave him a special place in the sky. Look north on a clear night: the steady star that never moves is called Dhruva Tara, the Pole Star.
text.hinglish: Dhruv ghar lauta, aur pita ne baahein phailaakar uska swagat kiya. Bada hokar woh dayaalu aur nyaayi raja bana. Aur Bhagwan Vishnu ne use aasmaan mein khaas jagah di. Saaf raat mein uttar ki taraf dekhiye: jo taara kabhi nahi hilta, use Dhruv Tara kehte hain.

moral.en: A small person with a steady heart can do great things. Determination shines like a star.
moral.hinglish: Atal mann wala chhota sa insaan bhi bade kaam kar sakta hai. Sankalp taare ki tarah chamakta hai.

reflection.en: When have you kept going even when something was hard?
reflection.hinglish: Kab aapne kathin hone par bhi haar nahi maani?

q.en: Dhruva's mother told him to keep anger in his heart.
q.hinglish: Dhruv ki maa ne kaha dil mein gussa rakho.

q.en: Narada tested Dhruva in the forest.
q.hinglish: Narad ne jungle mein Dhruv ko parkha.

q.en: The Pole Star is called Dhruva Tara.
q.hinglish: Pole Star ko Dhruv Tara kehte hain.

text.en: Long ago lived a proud king named Hiranyakashipu. He had a special boon and believed no one could ever defeat him. 'I am greater than God,' he said. 'Everyone must pray only to me.' The people were afraid, so they did as he said.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle Hiranyakashipu naam ka ek ghamandi raja tha. Uske paas ek khaas vardaan tha aur use lagta tha koi use kabhi nahi haraa sakta. 'Main Bhagwan se bhi bada hoon,' woh kehta. 'Sab sirf meri puja karein.' Log darte the, isliye maan jaate the.

text.en: But his own little son, Prahlad, was different. Prahlad had a gentle heart, and he loved Lord Vishnu. He sang Vishnu's name while playing, while eating, and before sleeping. 'Narayana, Narayana,' he would hum, smiling.
text.hinglish: Par uska apna nanha beta, Prahlad, alag tha. Prahlad ka dil komal tha aur use Bhagwan Vishnu se prem tha. Woh khelte, khaate aur sote samay Vishnu ka naam gaata. 'Narayan, Narayan,' woh muskuraate hue gungunaata.

text.en: The king was angry. 'Stop saying that name!' But Prahlad answered politely, 'Father, I love you. And I love Vishnu too. He is everywhere, in you, in me, in every pillar of this palace.' He was never rude, but he never gave up what he believed.
text.hinglish: Raja ko gussa aaya. 'Woh naam lena band karo!' Par Prahlad ne vinamrata se kaha, 'Pitaji, main aapse pyaar karta hoon. Aur Vishnu se bhi. Woh har jagah hain, aap mein, mujh mein, is mahal ke har khambe mein.' Woh kabhi badtameez nahi hua, par apni aastha nahi chhodi.

text.en: The king's sister Holika had a shawl that could not burn. She sat in a fire with Prahlad on her lap, wrapped in the shawl. But a wind blew the shawl from Holika onto Prahlad. Prahlad stepped out safe, still singing, and the fire took Holika instead. That is why we light the Holika fire the night before Holi.
text.hinglish: Raja ki behen Holika ke paas ek aisi chaadar thi jo jal nahi sakti thi. Woh Prahlad ko god mein lekar, chaadar odh kar aag mein baith gayi. Par hawa chali aur chaadar Holika se udkar Prahlad par aa gayi. Prahlad gaate hue surakshit bahar aa gaya, aur aag ne Holika ko le liya. Isiliye Holi se pehli raat Holika jalaate hain.

text.en: Finally the king shouted, 'Is your Vishnu in this pillar too?' Prahlad nodded calmly. The pillar cracked open, and Lord Vishnu came out as Narasimha, half lion and half man, to protect his young devotee. The proud king's reign was over.
text.hinglish: Aakhir raja chillaaya, 'Kya tumhara Vishnu is khambe mein bhi hai?' Prahlad ne shaanti se sir hilaaya. Khamba phat gaya, aur Bhagwan Vishnu Narsingh roop mein, aadhe sher aur aadhe manushya, apne nanhe bhakt ki raksha ke liye prakat hue. Ghamandi raja ka raaj khatam hua.

text.en: Prahlad grew up to be a wise and kind king. Every Holi, when we play with colours, we remember a little boy who stayed gentle and brave, who never hated anyone, and who believed that goodness is stronger than pride.
text.hinglish: Prahlad bada hokar ek samajhdaar aur dayaalu raja bana. Har Holi, jab hum rang khelte hain, hum us nanhe baalak ko yaad karte hain jo komal aur bahadur raha, jisne kabhi kisi se nafrat nahi ki, aur jise vishvaas tha ki achhaai ghamand se zyada taakatvar hai.

say.en: Little one, be gentle and be brave. Goodness is always stronger.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, komal rehna aur bahadur rehna. Achhaai hamesha zyada taakatvar hai.

moral.en: Be gentle and polite, and stay true to what is good, even when it is hard.
moral.hinglish: Komal aur vinamra raho, aur kathin ho tab bhi achhaai par tike raho.

reflection.en: What goodness would you like your baby to hold on to always?
reflection.hinglish: Aap chahengi baby hamesha kaun si achhaai pakde rahe?

q.en: Prahlad was rude to his father.
q.hinglish: Prahlad apne pita se badtameezi karta tha.

q.en: Holika's shawl flew onto Prahlad and kept him safe.
q.hinglish: Holika ki chaadar udkar Prahlad par aa gayi aur use bachaaya.

q.en: Narasimha was half lion and half man.
q.hinglish: Narsingh aadhe sher aur aadhe manushya the.

text.en: In the village of Gokul, the mornings smelled of fresh milk. Mother Yashoda churned curd in a big matka, singing as the butter rose. And somewhere nearby, a little boy with a peacock feather in his hair was watching very, very carefully.
text.hinglish: Gokul gaon mein subah taaze doodh ki khushboo aati thi. Maa Yashoda bade matke mein dahi bilote hue gaati, aur makhan upar aata. Aur paas hi kahin, baalon mein mor pankh lagaaye ek nanha baalak bahut dhyaan se dekh raha tha.

text.en: That boy was Krishna, and he loved butter more than anything. When Yashoda went to fetch water, Krishna called his friends. They made a tower: one friend on the bottom, one in the middle, and little Krishna on top, reaching for the pot hanging from the ceiling.
text.hinglish: Woh baalak the Krishna, aur unhe makhan sabse zyada pasand tha. Jab Yashoda paani lene gayi, Krishna ne doston ko bulaaya. Unhone meenar banaayi: ek dost neeche, ek beech mein, aur nanhe Krishna sabse upar, chhat se latke matke tak haath badhaate hue.

text.en: Down came the butter, and everyone shared it, even the monkeys at the window! When Yashoda came back, she found butter on the floor, butter on the monkeys, and butter all over Krishna's round cheeks.
text.hinglish: Makhan neeche aaya, aur sabne baanta, khidki par baithe bandaron ne bhi! Jab Yashoda lauti, to farsh par makhan, bandaron par makhan, aur Krishna ke gol-gol gaalon par makhan hi makhan tha.

text.en: 'Kanha! Did you eat the butter?' asked Yashoda, trying not to laugh. Krishna opened his big eyes wide. The poet Surdas wrote his famous reply: 'Maiya mori, main nahin makhan khayo!' Mother, I didn't eat the butter! The friends must have put it on my face!
text.hinglish: 'Kanha! Kya tumne makhan khaaya?' Yashoda ne hansi rokte hue poochha. Krishna ne apni badi-badi aankhein kholi. Kavi Surdas ne unka prasiddh jawaab likha: 'Maiya mori, main nahin makhan khayo!' Maa, maine makhan nahi khaaya! Doston ne mere munh par laga diya hoga!

text.en: Yashoda pretended to be strict, but her heart melted like warm butter. She picked him up, wiped his face with her dupatta, and kissed his cheeks. Then she said gently, 'Next time, just ask me, my little thief. I will always share with you.'
text.hinglish: Yashoda ne sakht hone ka naatak kiya, par unka dil garm makhan ki tarah pighal gaya. Unhone use god mein uthaaya, dupatte se munh poncha aur gaal choome. Phir pyaar se boli, 'Agli baar bas maang lena, mere nanhe chor. Main hamesha tumhare saath baantungi.'

say.en: Little one, my love for you is softer than butter and sweeter than mishri.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, mera pyaar makhan se naram aur mishri se meetha hai.

text.en: From that day, Krishna was called Makhan Chor, the butter thief, with lots of love. On Janmashtami, families still hang a matka of butter high up for the dahi-handi. And mothers still smile, remembering that every child is a little Kanha.
text.hinglish: Us din se Krishna ko pyaar se Makhan Chor kaha jaane laga. Janmashtami par aaj bhi parivaar dahi-handi ke liye makhan ka matka ooncha latkaate hain. Aur maayein muskuraati hain, yaad karke ki har bachcha ek nanha Kanha hai.

moral.en: Sharing brings joy, honesty matters, and a mother's love forgives with a smile.
moral.hinglish: Baantne se khushi milti hai, sach bolna zaroori hai, aur maa ka pyaar muskura kar maaf karta hai.

reflection.en: What playful thing do you imagine your baby doing one day?
reflection.hinglish: Aap sochti hain baby ek din kaun si natkhat harkat karega?

q.en: Krishna and his friends made a tower to reach the butter.
q.hinglish: Krishna aur doston ne makhan tak pahunchne ke liye meenar banaayi.

q.en: Surdas wrote 'Maiya mori, main nahin makhan khayo'.
q.hinglish: Surdas ne likha 'Maiya mori, main nahin makhan khayo'.

q.en: Yashoda stopped loving Krishna after the butter was gone.
q.hinglish: Makhan khatam hone ke baad Yashoda ne Krishna se pyaar karna chhod diya.

text.en: In a forest lived a boy named Eklavya. He dreamed of becoming a great archer. He walked to the school of Guru Dronacharya, the famous teacher of the princes. But Drona said, 'I teach only the princes of Hastinapur.' Eklavya bowed and went back to the forest.
text.hinglish: Ek jungle mein Eklavya naam ka ladka rehta tha. Uska sapna tha mahaan dhanurdhar banna. Woh Guru Dronacharya ke ashram gaya, jo rajkumaron ke prasiddh guru the. Par Drona ne kaha, 'Main sirf Hastinapur ke rajkumaron ko padhaata hoon.' Eklavya ne pranaam kiya aur jungle laut gaya.

text.en: He was not angry. Instead, he made a statue of Drona from clay and placed it under a tree. Every morning he bowed to the statue and said, 'Guruji, please teach me.' Then he practised, from sunrise until the stars came out.
text.hinglish: Woh naaraz nahi hua. Usne mitti se Drona ki moorti banaayi aur ek ped ke neeche rakh di. Har subah moorti ko pranaam karke kehta, 'Guruji, mujhe sikhaaiye.' Phir suraj nikalne se taare aane tak abhyaas karta.

question.en: Eklavya couldn't join the school. What could he do?
question.hinglish: Eklavya ashram mein nahi ja saka. Woh kya kar sakta tha?

label.en: Practise on his own every day
label.hinglish: Roz khud abhyaas kare

lesson.en: That's what he did! A teacher's lessons can live in our hearts. Daily practice builds great skill.
lesson.hinglish: Usne yahi kiya! Guru ki seekh dil mein reh sakti hai. Roz ka abhyaas badi kala banata hai.

label.en: Learn by watching others carefully
label.hinglish: Doosron ko dhyaan se dekhkar seekhe

lesson.en: A great idea! Watching, listening and copying are powerful ways to learn, just like a baby learning from its family.
lesson.hinglish: Badhiya soch! Dekhna, sunna aur nakal karna seekhne ke shaktishaali tareeke hain, jaise baby parivaar se seekhta hai.

text.en: Days became months, months became years. Eklavya's arrows began to fly true. He could hit a leaf spinning in the wind. He became so skilled that even the animals of the forest watched him with wonder.
text.hinglish: Din mahine bane, mahine saal. Eklavya ke teer seedhe udne lage. Woh hawa mein ghoomte patte ko bhi bhed sakta tha. Woh itna kushal ho gaya ki jungle ke jaanwar bhi use hairaani se dekhte.

text.en: One day, Drona and the princes came to the forest. They saw Eklavya's amazing skill. 'Who taught you?' asked Drona. Eklavya bowed and pointed to the clay statue. 'You did, Guruji. I learned in front of your image.'
text.hinglish: Ek din Drona aur rajkumar jungle aaye. Unhone Eklavya ka adbhut hunar dekha. 'Tumhe kisne sikhaaya?' Drona ne poochha. Eklavya ne jhukkar mitti ki moorti ki taraf ishaara kiya. 'Aapne, Guruji. Maine aapki moorti ke saamne seekha.'

text.en: In those days, a student offered guru dakshina, a gift to the teacher. Drona asked Eklavya for his right thumb. Without a moment's doubt, Eklavya gave it with a smile, because he respected his guru so deeply. Then, the old stories say, he kept practising and learned to shoot in a new way.
text.hinglish: Us zamaane mein shishya guru ko guru dakshina deta tha. Drona ne Eklavya se uska daayaan angootha maanga. Bina ek pal soche, Eklavya ne muskura kar de diya, kyonki woh guru ka itna aadar karta tha. Phir, puraani kahaniyan kehti hain, usne abhyaas jaari rakha aur naye tareeke se teer chalaana seekha.

text.en: Today, Eklavya is remembered across India as the student with the greatest dedication. He shows us that if the door is closed, we can still learn with focus, respect and daily practice. Nothing can stop a heart that truly wants to learn.
text.hinglish: Aaj poore Bharat mein Eklavya ko sabse lagan wale shishya ke roop mein yaad kiya jaata hai. Woh sikhaata hai ki darwaza band ho tab bhi dhyaan, aadar aur roz ke abhyaas se seekha ja sakta hai. Jo dil sach mein seekhna chahta hai, use koi nahi rok sakta.

say.en: Little one, you will learn so many wonderful things, one small step every day.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum roz ek chhote kadam se bahut saari pyaari cheezein seekhoge.

moral.en: With dedication, respect and daily practice, we can learn almost anything.
moral.hinglish: Lagan, aadar aur roz ke abhyaas se hum lagbhag kuch bhi seekh sakte hain.

reflection.en: What would you love to learn alongside your child one day?
reflection.hinglish: Aap ek din apne bachche ke saath kya seekhna chahengi?

q.en: Eklavya made a clay statue of his guru.
q.hinglish: Eklavya ne guru ki mitti ki moorti banaayi.

q.en: Eklavya stopped practising when he couldn't join the school.
q.hinglish: Ashram na milne par Eklavya ne abhyaas chhod diya.

q.en: Eklavya is remembered for his dedication.
q.hinglish: Eklavya ko uski lagan ke liye yaad kiya jaata hai.

title.en: Kalpana Chawla: from Karnal to the stars
title.hinglish: Kalpana Chawla: Karnal se taaron tak

text.en: In Karnal, a town in Haryana, there lived a little girl named Kalpana. On warm summer nights, the family slept on the rooftop. While others fell asleep, Kalpana looked up at the stars and wondered, 'What is up there? How far does the sky go?'
text.hinglish: Haryana ke Karnal shehar mein Kalpana naam ki ek nanhi ladki rehti thi. Garmi ki raaton mein parivaar chhat par sota tha. Jab sab so jaate, Kalpana taaron ko dekhkar sochti, 'Upar kya hai? Aasmaan kitni door tak jaata hai?'

text.en: Kalpana loved drawing aeroplanes at school. She watched the small planes at the Karnal flying club with shining eyes. Some people said, 'Engineering is not for girls.' But Kalpana's family believed in her, and she believed in herself.
text.hinglish: Kalpana ko school mein hawaai jahaaz banaana bahut pasand tha. Woh Karnal flying club ke chhote jahaazon ko chamakti aankhon se dekhti. Kuch log kehte, 'Engineering ladkiyon ke liye nahi hai.' Par Kalpana ke parivaar ko us par bharosa tha, aur use khud par.

text.en: She studied aeronautical engineering at Punjab Engineering College in Chandigarh. Then she went to America to study more, and earned a PhD. She also learned to fly planes herself. Every step took years of hard work and patience.
text.hinglish: Usne Chandigarh ke Punjab Engineering College mein aeronautical engineering padhi. Phir aage padhne America gayi aur PhD ki. Usne khud jahaaz udaana bhi seekha. Har kadam par saalon ki mehnat aur dheeraj laga.

question.en: Someone tells Kalpana, 'This dream is too big for a girl from a small town.' What should she do?
question.hinglish: Koi Kalpana se kehta hai, 'Chhote shehar ki ladki ke liye yeh sapna bahut bada hai.' Use kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Keep studying quietly and prove it with work
label.hinglish: Chupchaap padhti rahe aur kaam se dikhaaye

lesson.en: That's what Kalpana did. Hard work spoke louder than any words.
lesson.hinglish: Kalpana ne yahi kiya. Mehnat ne har baat se zyada zor se jawaab diya.

label.en: Find people who believe in her dream
label.hinglish: Unse jude jo uske sapne par bharosa karein

lesson.en: Lovely! Her family and teachers cheered her on. The right people help our dreams grow wings.
lesson.hinglish: Badhiya! Parivaar aur shikshakon ne uska hausla badhaaya. Sahi log sapnon ko pankh dete hain.

text.en: NASA, America's space agency, chose her to be an astronaut. In 1997, Kalpana flew on the space shuttle Columbia. She became the first woman born in India to go to space. From up there, she said, she could see the whole Earth, and it looked like one home for everyone.
text.hinglish: NASA, America ki antariksh sanstha, ne use antariksh yaatri chuna. 1997 mein Kalpana space shuttle Columbia mein udi. Woh antariksh jaane wali Bharat mein janmi pehli mahila bani. Wahan se, usne kaha, poori dharti dikhti thi, aur woh sabka ek ghar lagti thi.

text.en: Kalpana went to space a second time in 2003. On the way home, the shuttle Columbia was lost, and India and the world grieved. But her light did not go out. Schools, scholarships and even an Indian weather satellite, Kalpana-1, carry her name.
text.hinglish: 2003 mein Kalpana doosri baar antariksh gayi. Wapas aate samay shuttle Columbia kho gaya, aur Bharat aur duniya dukhi hue. Par uski roshni nahi bujhi. School, scholarship aur ek Bhartiya mausam satellite, Kalpana-1, uske naam par hain.

text.en: Today, girls and boys in Karnal and all over Haryana look up at the night sky and think of her. Kalpana showed that a child from a small town, with curiosity, courage and hard work, can reach the stars.
text.hinglish: Aaj Karnal aur poore Haryana ke ladke-ladkiyan raat ke aasmaan ko dekhkar use yaad karte hain. Kalpana ne dikhaaya ki chhote shehar ka bachcha bhi, jigyaasa, himmat aur mehnat se, taaron tak pahunch sakta hai.

say.en: Little one, dream as big as the sky. We will be right beside you.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, aasmaan jitne bade sapne dekhna. Hum hamesha tumhare saath rahenge.

moral.en: Curiosity, courage and steady hard work can take you from a small town to the stars.
moral.hinglish: Jigyaasa, himmat aur lagaataar mehnat chhote shehar se taaron tak le ja sakti hai.

reflection.en: What big dream would you love to cheer your child on for?
reflection.hinglish: Aap apne bachche ke kis bade sapne ka hausla badhaana chahengi?

q.en: Kalpana Chawla grew up in Karnal, Haryana.
q.hinglish: Kalpana Chawla Karnal, Haryana mein badi hui.

q.en: She first flew to space in 1997 on Columbia.
q.hinglish: Woh pehli baar 1997 mein Columbia se antariksh gayi.

q.en: Kalpana gave up when people said engineering was not for girls.
q.hinglish: Logon ke kehne par Kalpana ne engineering chhod di.

title.en: Daughters of Haryana: the Phogat sisters and Saina
title.hinglish: Haryana ki betiyan: Phogat behnein aur Saina

text.en: In the village of Balali in Bhiwani district lived a wrestler named Mahavir Singh Phogat. He watched his daughters Geeta and Babita run and play, and he saw strength in them. He decided to train them in kushti, wrestling, the sport of Haryana's akhadas.
text.hinglish: Bhiwani zile ke Balali gaon mein Mahavir Singh Phogat naam ke pehlwaan rehte the. Unhone apni betiyon Geeta aur Babita ko daudte-khelte dekha, aur unmein taakat dekhi. Unhone tay kiya ki unhe kushti sikhaayenge, Haryana ke akhadon ka khel.

text.en: Some people in the village said, 'Wrestling is not for girls.' But the girls woke before sunrise, ran in the fields, and practised on the mud floor, day after day, in the cold of winter and the heat of summer. They often trained with boys, because there were few girls wrestling then.
text.hinglish: Gaon ke kuch log kehte, 'Kushti ladkiyon ka khel nahi.' Par ladkiyan suraj nikalne se pehle uthti, kheton mein daudti, aur mitti ke akhade mein roz abhyaas karti, sardi ki thand aur garmi ki tapti dhoop mein. Aksar ladkon ke saath ladti, kyonki tab bahut kam ladkiyan kushti karti thi.

question.en: People say girls can't wrestle. What should Geeta do?
question.hinglish: Log kehte hain ladkiyan kushti nahi kar sakti. Geeta ko kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Train harder and let her wins speak
label.hinglish: Aur mehnat kare aur jeet se jawaab de

lesson.en: That's exactly what happened! Her medals answered everyone.
lesson.hinglish: Bilkul yahi hua! Uske medalon ne sabko jawaab de diya.

label.en: Stay close to the people who support her
label.hinglish: Saath dene walon ke paas rahe

lesson.en: Yes! Her father and sisters trained together and lifted each other up. Family support is a superpower.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Pita aur behnon ne saath abhyaas kiya aur ek-doosre ka hausla badhaaya. Parivaar ka saath ek super-shakti hai.

text.en: Their hard work paid off. At the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi, Geeta Phogat won gold, the first Indian woman wrestler to do so. In 2012 she became the first Indian woman wrestler to qualify for the Olympics. Babita won Commonwealth gold in 2014.
text.hinglish: Unki mehnat rang laayi. 2010 ke Delhi Commonwealth Games mein Geeta Phogat ne gold jeeta, aisa karne wali pehli Bhartiya mahila pehlwaan. 2012 mein woh Olympics ke liye qualify karne wali pehli Bhartiya mahila pehlwaan bani. Babita ne 2014 mein Commonwealth gold jeeta.

text.en: Their younger sisters and cousins took up wrestling too. Soon, girls all over Haryana were joining akhadas. The same villagers who had doubted now cheered loudest. One family's courage changed what a whole state believed girls could do.
text.hinglish: Unki chhoti behnein aur cousins bhi kushti mein aayi. Jaldi hi poore Haryana mein ladkiyan akhadon mein jaane lagi. Jo gaon wale shak karte the, ab sabse zor se taali bajaate. Ek parivaar ki himmat ne poore pradesh ki soch badal di.

text.en: Another daughter of Haryana, Saina Nehwal, was born in Hisar. She played badminton with focus and grace. At the 2012 London Olympics she won a bronze medal, India's first Olympic medal in badminton, and in 2015 she became world number one.
text.hinglish: Haryana ki ek aur beti, Saina Nehwal, Hisar mein paida hui. Woh dhyaan aur sundarta se badminton khelti thi. 2012 London Olympics mein usne bronze jeeta, badminton mein Bharat ka pehla Olympic medal, aur 2015 mein woh duniya mein number ek bani.

text.en: These daughters of Haryana teach us something beautiful: courage grows with practice, and a family's belief can open doors that were closed for years. Every child, laado or laadla, deserves that belief.
text.hinglish: Haryana ki yeh betiyan ek sundar baat sikhaati hain: himmat abhyaas se badhti hai, aur parivaar ka bharosa saalon se band darwaaze khol sakta hai. Har bachcha, laado ho ya laadla, us bharose ka haqdaar hai.

say.en: Little one, whoever you grow up to be, we will believe in you every single day.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum bade hokar jo bhi bano, hum har din tum par bharosa karenge.

moral.en: Practice builds courage, and a family's belief helps every child shine.
moral.hinglish: Abhyaas himmat banata hai, aur parivaar ka bharosa har bachche ko chamkaata hai.

reflection.en: How will your family cheer your child on, whatever they choose to do?
reflection.hinglish: Aapka parivaar bachche ka hausla kaise badhaayega, woh jo bhi chune?

q.en: Geeta Phogat won gold at the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi.
q.hinglish: Geeta Phogat ne 2010 Delhi Commonwealth Games mein gold jeeta.

q.en: Saina Nehwal was born in Hisar.
q.hinglish: Saina Nehwal Hisar mein paida hui.

q.en: The Phogat sisters trained only when the weather was nice.
q.hinglish: Phogat behnein sirf achhe mausam mein abhyaas karti thi.

title.en: The clever rabbit and the lion (Panchatantra)

text.en: In a thick forest lived a huge, proud lion named Bhasuraka. Every day he hunted far more than he needed. The animals were frightened, so they met under a banyan tree and made a deal with him: 'Stay in your den. Each day, one of us will come to you.'
text.hinglish: Ek ghane jungle mein Bhasurak naam ka ek bada, ghamandi sher rehta tha. Woh roz zaroorat se zyada shikaar karta. Jaanwar dar gaye, to bargad ke neeche mile aur sher se samjhauta kiya: 'Aap apni gufa mein rahiye. Roz hum mein se ek aapke paas aayega.'

text.en: One day it was the turn of a small rabbit. The rabbit's legs shook, but his mind was busy. 'Being small doesn't mean being helpless,' he thought. 'I have a brain, and I will use it.' He walked very, very slowly to the lion's den.
text.hinglish: Ek din ek chhote khargosh ki baari aayi. Khargosh ke pair kaanp rahe the, par dimaag tez chal raha tha. 'Chhota hone ka matlab bebas hona nahi,' usne socha. 'Mere paas dimaag hai, main uska istemaal karoonga.' Woh bahut dheere-dheere sher ki gufa ki taraf gaya.

question.en: The rabbit is small and scared. What can he use to stay safe?
question.hinglish: Khargosh chhota aur dara hua hai. Woh surakshit rehne ke liye kya istemaal kar sakta hai?

label.en: His clever thinking
label.hinglish: Apni chatur soch

lesson.en: Yes! Thinking calmly is a superpower, even for the smallest creature.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Shaanti se sochna super-shakti hai, sabse chhote jeev ke liye bhi.

label.en: Patience: going slowly to think of a plan
label.hinglish: Dheeraj: dheere chalkar yojana sochna

lesson.en: Wise! By taking his time, the rabbit gave his mind room to find a plan.
lesson.hinglish: Samajhdaari! Samay lekar khargosh ne dimaag ko yojana dhoondhne ka mauka diya.

text.en: The lion roared, 'You're late, and you're tiny!' The rabbit bowed. 'Maharaj, five rabbits were coming for you. But on the way, another lion stopped us. He said he is the real king of this forest. Only I escaped to tell you.'
text.hinglish: Sher garja, 'Tum der se aaye ho, aur itne chhote ho!' Khargosh ne sir jhukaaya. 'Maharaj, paanch khargosh aapke liye aa rahe the. Par raaste mein ek doosre sher ne hume rok liya. Usne kaha woh is jungle ka asli raja hai. Bas main bachkar aapko bataane aaya hoon.'

text.en: 'Another king? In MY forest?' the lion roared. 'Show me this lion!' The rabbit led him to an old, deep well. 'He lives down there, Maharaj.' The lion looked in and saw a lion's face looking back, angry and roaring. It was only his own reflection in the water!
text.hinglish: 'Doosra raja? MERE jungle mein?' sher daha. 'Mujhe dikhao woh sher!' Khargosh use ek puraane, gehre kuein tak le gaya. 'Woh neeche rehta hai, Maharaj.' Sher ne jhaanka aur ek gusse wala, dahadta sher dikha. Woh paani mein uski apni parchhaai thi!

text.en: The proud lion roared at the reflection, and the reflection seemed to roar back. In a rage, he leapt into the well with a great splash, and he never troubled the forest again. The little rabbit hopped home, and all the animals cheered under the banyan tree.
text.hinglish: Ghamandi sher parchhaai par garja, aur parchhaai bhi garajti lagi. Gusse mein woh zor ki chhapak ke saath kuein mein kood gaya, aur phir kabhi jungle ko pareshaan nahi kiya. Nanha khargosh uchhalta ghar aaya, aur bargad ke neeche saare jaanwaron ne khushi manaayi.

text.en: Vishnu Sharma wrote the Panchatantra long ago to teach young princes wisdom through animal stories. The clever rabbit reminds us: a calm mind is stronger than a loud roar.
text.hinglish: Vishnu Sharma ne bahut pehle rajkumaron ko jaanwaron ki kahaniyon se samajh sikhaane ke liye Panchatantra likha. Chatur khargosh yaad dilaata hai: shaant dimaag zor ki dahaad se zyada taakatvar hai.

say.en: Little one, stay calm and think. You are cleverer than you know.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, shaant rehkar socho. Tum apni soch se bhi zyada samajhdaar ho.

moral.en: A calm, clever mind is stronger than size or a loud roar.
moral.hinglish: Shaant, chatur dimaag aakaar aur tez dahaad se zyada taakatvar hai.

reflection.en: When did staying calm help you solve a problem?
reflection.hinglish: Kab shaant rehne se aapki koi pareshaani suljhi?

q.en: The rabbit used his clever thinking.
q.hinglish: Khargosh ne apni chatur soch ka istemaal kiya.

q.en: There really was another lion in the well.
q.hinglish: Kuein mein sach mein doosra sher tha.

q.en: The Panchatantra was written by Vishnu Sharma.
q.hinglish: Panchatantra Vishnu Sharma ne likha.

text.en: Princess Savitri was wise, kind and brave. When it was time to marry, she chose Satyavan, a gentle young man who lived in the forest and cared for his blind parents. Savitri loved his honest heart.
text.hinglish: Rajkumari Savitri samajhdaar, dayaalu aur bahadur thi. Vivaah ka samay aaya to usne Satyavan ko chuna, ek komal yuvak jo jungle mein rehta tha aur apne andhe maata-pita ki seva karta tha. Savitri ko uska sachcha dil pasand tha.

text.en: The sage Narada warned her: 'Satyavan is good, but his life will be short.' Savitri listened calmly. 'I have chosen with my heart,' she said. 'I will face whatever comes, with courage and with prayer.'
text.hinglish: Narad Muni ne chetaavni di: 'Satyavan achha hai, par uska jeevan chhota hoga.' Savitri ne shaanti se suna. 'Maine dil se chuna hai,' woh boli. 'Jo bhi aaye, himmat aur prarthana se saamna karoongi.'

text.en: One day, under a big banyan tree, Satyavan felt tired and laid his head on her lap. Then Yamraj, the calm and fair lord of life's ending, came to take Satyavan's spirit. Savitri stood up and quietly followed him.
text.hinglish: Ek din, ek bade bargad ke neeche, Satyavan thak kar uski god mein sir rakh kar let gaya. Tab Yamraj, jeevan ke ant ke shaant aur nyaayi devta, Satyavan ki aatma lene aaye. Savitri uthi aur chupchaap unke peeche chal padi.

text.en: 'Go back, child,' said Yamraj. But Savitri spoke such wise and gentle words about truth and duty that Yamraj was pleased. 'Ask me for a boon,' he said, 'anything except Satyavan's life.' Savitri asked for her father-in-law's eyesight. 'Granted.'
text.hinglish: 'Laut jao, beti,' Yamraj bole. Par Savitri ne satya aur kartavya par itni samajhdaar aur komal baatein kahi ki Yamraj prasann ho gaye. 'Ek var maango,' unhone kaha, 'Satyavan ke jeevan ke alaawa kuch bhi.' Savitri ne sasur ki aankhon ki roshni maangi. 'Tathaastu.'

question.en: Yamraj offers one more boon. What could wise Savitri ask for?
question.hinglish: Yamraj ek aur var dete hain. Samajhdaar Savitri kya maang sakti hai?

label.en: Children with Satyavan
label.hinglish: Satyavan ke saath santaan

lesson.en: That's exactly what she asked! And Yamraj, true to his word, had to give Satyavan's life back. Wisdom found a way.
lesson.hinglish: Usne bilkul yahi maanga! Aur Yamraj ko, apne vachan ke anusaar, Satyavan ka jeevan lautaana pada. Samajh ne raasta nikaala.

label.en: Happiness for her family
label.hinglish: Parivaar ki khushi

lesson.en: A loving wish! Savitri also asked for her in-laws' lost kingdom back. Then, with one clever boon, she won Satyavan's life too.
lesson.hinglish: Pyaari khwaahish! Savitri ne sasuraal ka khoya raajya bhi maanga. Phir ek chatur var se Satyavan ka jeevan bhi jeet liya.

text.en: Savitri asked, 'Bless me to have children with Satyavan.' Yamraj said 'Granted' before he realised: for that, Satyavan must live! He smiled at her wisdom and returned Satyavan's life. Satyavan opened his eyes under the banyan tree, as if waking from a nap.
text.hinglish: Savitri ne kaha, 'Mujhe Satyavan ke saath santaan ka aashirvaad dijiye.' Yamraj ne samajhne se pehle hi 'Tathaastu' keh diya: iske liye to Satyavan ka jeevit rehna zaroori tha! Woh uski samajh par muskuraaye aur Satyavan ka jeevan lauta diya. Satyavan ne bargad ke neeche aankhein kholi, jaise jhapki se jaage hon.

text.en: That is why many women in Haryana and across India tie threads around a banyan tree on Vat Savitri. Savitri reminds us that calm words, love and a clear mind can change even the hardest moments.
text.hinglish: Isiliye Haryana aur poore Bharat mein kai mahilayein Vat Savitri par bargad ke ped par dhaaga baandhti hain. Savitri yaad dilaati hai ki shaant shabd, pyaar aur saaf dimaag sabse kathin pal bhi badal sakte hain.

say.en: Little one, may you always have a wise mind and a loving heart, like Savitri.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, tumhara mann Savitri jaisa samajhdaar aur dil pyaar bhara ho.

moral.en: Calm, wise words and steady love can find a way through the hardest times.
moral.hinglish: Shaant, samajhdaar shabd aur atal pyaar sabse kathin samay mein bhi raasta nikaal lete hain.

reflection.en: Who in your life always finds the right words? What would you like to learn from them?
reflection.hinglish: Aapke jeevan mein kaun hamesha sahi shabd dhoondh leta hai? Aap unse kya seekhna chahengi?

q.en: Savitri followed Yamraj and spoke with him wisely.
q.hinglish: Savitri Yamraj ke peeche gayi aur samajhdaari se baat ki.

q.en: Savitri shouted at Yamraj until he gave up.
q.hinglish: Savitri Yamraj par tab tak chillaayi jab tak woh haar nahi gaye.

q.en: Vat Savitri is linked with the banyan tree.
q.hinglish: Vat Savitri bargad ke ped se juda hai.

text.en: Long ago, in the forests near the mountains, Mother Anjana had a baby boy full of energy. He giggled at birds, tumbled with deer, and climbed trees faster than the monkeys. Pawan Dev, the god of the wind, loved him like his own son.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle, pahaadon ke paas ke jungle mein, Maa Anjana ka ek bahut chanchal beta tha. Woh chidiyon par khilkhilaata, hiranon ke saath lotta, aur bandaron se bhi tez pedon par chadhta. Hawa ke devta Pawan Dev use apne bete jaisa pyaar karte the.

text.en: One morning the baby woke up hungry. He looked up and saw the rising sun, round, orange and glowing. 'What a big, juicy mango!' he thought. And with one mighty jump, he flew up into the sky to pick it.
text.hinglish: Ek subah baalak bhookha jaaga. Usne upar ugta suraj dekha, gol, naarangi aur chamakta. 'Kitna bada, raseela aam!' usne socha. Aur ek zabardast chhalaang lagaakar, woh use todne aasmaan mein ud gaya.

text.en: The gods were amazed and a little worried. Indra Dev gently stopped him, and his thunderbolt touched the baby's chin, which is called 'hanu'. From that day the child was called Hanuman, the one with the special chin.
text.hinglish: Devta hairaan bhi hue aur thode chintit bhi. Indra Dev ne use dheere se roka, aur unka vajra baalak ki thodi ko chhoo gaya, jise 'hanu' kehte hain. Us din se baalak ka naam pada Hanuman, khaas thodi wala.

text.en: Pawan Dev hugged Hanuman close, and all the gods came to bless him. One gave strength, one gave wisdom, one gave the power to grow big or small. The little monkey child became the bravest, kindest helper the world has known.
text.hinglish: Pawan Dev ne Hanuman ko seene se lagaaya, aur saare devta aashirvaad dene aaye. Kisi ne shakti di, kisi ne buddhi, kisi ne bada ya chhota hone ki shakti. Nanha baalak duniya ka sabse bahadur aur dayaalu sevak bana.

text.en: Hanuman never used his strength to show off. He used it to help: to serve Shri Ram, to protect the weak, to keep his promises. Even today, families say 'Jai Hanuman' when they need courage.
text.hinglish: Hanuman ne apni taakat kabhi dikhaave ke liye nahi lagaayi. Unhone madad ke liye lagaayi: Shri Ram ki seva, kamzor ki raksha, vaade nibhaane mein. Aaj bhi parivaar himmat chahiye to 'Jai Hanuman' kehte hain.

say.en: Little one, may you be strong like Hanuman, and use your strength to help others.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, Hanuman jaise taakatvar bano, aur apni taakat se doosron ki madad karo.

moral.en: Curiosity and energy are gifts; strength is most beautiful when it is used to help.
moral.hinglish: Jigyaasa aur josh vardaan hain; taakat tab sabse sundar hai jab madad mein lage.

reflection.en: What playful thing do you think your baby will be curious about first?
reflection.hinglish: Aapko lagta hai baby sabse pehle kis cheez ke baare mein jigyaasu hoga?

q.en: Baby Hanuman thought the sun was a mango.
q.hinglish: Baal Hanuman ne suraj ko aam samjha.

q.en: Hanuman used his strength to show off.
q.hinglish: Hanuman ne taakat dikhaave ke liye lagaayi.

q.en: Pawan Dev is the god of the wind.
q.hinglish: Pawan Dev hawa ke devta hain.

title.en: Shri Ram and the little squirrel

text.en: To bring Sita home, Shri Ram's army had to cross the wide sea to Lanka. The vanar sena, the monkey and bear army, decided to build a bridge. Strong monkeys carried huge rocks, wrote 'Ram' on them, and the stones floated on the water!
text.hinglish: Sita ji ko wapas laane ke liye Shri Ram ki sena ko chauda samudra paar karke Lanka jaana tha. Vanar sena ne pul banaane ka faisla kiya. Taakatvar vanar badi-badi chattaanein laaye, un par 'Ram' likha, aur pathar paani par tairne lage!

text.en: Among all the giants worked a tiny squirrel. She ran into the water, rolled in the sand on the beach, then ran onto the bridge and shook the sand off between the stones. Back and forth, back and forth, all day long.
text.hinglish: Un sab vishaal saathiyon ke beech ek nanhi gilahri bhi kaam kar rahi thi. Woh paani mein jaati, kinaare ki ret mein lotti, phir pul par jaakar pattharon ke beech ret jhaad deti. Idhar-udhar, idhar-udhar, din bhar.

text.en: A big monkey laughed. 'Move aside, little one! What can your few grains of sand do?' The squirrel was not upset. 'I can't carry rocks,' she said, 'but I can fill the small gaps. That is my part.'
text.hinglish: Ek bade vanar ne hansi udaayi. 'Hat jao, chhoti! Tumhare do daane ret se kya hoga?' Gilahri udaas nahi hui. 'Main chattaan nahi utha sakti,' woh boli, 'par chhote khaali jagah bhar sakti hoon. Yahi mera hissa hai.'

question.en: The big monkey laughs at the squirrel. What should she do?
question.hinglish: Bada vanar gilahri par hansta hai. Use kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Keep doing her small part happily
label.hinglish: Khushi se apna chhota kaam karti rahe

lesson.en: Yes! Small work done with love matters. Shri Ram noticed it.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Pyaar se kiya chhota kaam bhi maayne rakhta hai. Shri Ram ne dekha.

label.en: Gently explain why sand helps
label.hinglish: Pyaar se samjhaaye ki ret kyon zaroori hai

lesson.en: Lovely! Calm words helped the monkey see that sand fills gaps and makes the bridge strong.
lesson.hinglish: Bahut badhiya! Shaant baaton se vanar samajh gaya ki ret khaali jagah bharkar pul majboot karti hai.

text.en: Shri Ram saw everything. He picked up the squirrel tenderly and said, 'Every helper matters, big or small. Her sand holds the rocks together.' And he stroked her back lovingly with three fingers.
text.hinglish: Shri Ram sab dekh rahe the. Unhone gilahri ko pyaar se uthaaya aur kaha, 'Har madadgaar maayne rakhta hai, bada ho ya chhota. Iski ret hi pattharon ko jodti hai.' Aur unhone teen ungliyon se uski peeth pyaar se sehlaayi.

text.en: The old stories say that is why Indian squirrels have three soft stripes on their backs: the mark of Shri Ram's love. Next time you see one in the courtyard, remember the tiny helper.
text.hinglish: Puraani kahaniyan kehti hain isiliye Bhartiya gilahri ki peeth par teen komal dhaariyan hoti hain: Shri Ram ke pyaar ka nishaan. Agli baar aangan mein gilahri dikhe, to us nanhi madadgaar ko yaad kijiye.

say.en: Little one, no help is too small when it is given with love.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, pyaar se ki gayi koi bhi madad chhoti nahi hoti.

moral.en: Every small effort made with love counts.
moral.hinglish: Pyaar se kiya har chhota prayaas maayne rakhta hai.

reflection.en: What small thing did someone do for you this week that meant a lot?
reflection.hinglish: Is hafte kisi ne aapke liye kaun sa chhota kaam kiya jo bahut pyaara laga?

q.en: The squirrel carried big rocks.
q.hinglish: Gilahri ne badi chattaanein uthaayi.

q.en: Shri Ram said every helper matters.
q.hinglish: Shri Ram ne kaha har madadgaar maayne rakhta hai.

q.en: The stones floated because 'Ram' was written on them.
q.hinglish: Pattharon par 'Ram' likha tha isliye woh taire.

text.en: In a quiet forest ashram lived an old woman named Shabari. Her guru, Rishi Matang, had told her, 'One day Shri Ram will come to your door.' So every single morning, for many, many years, Shabari swept the path and waited.
text.hinglish: Ek shaant jungle ke ashram mein Shabari naam ki ek boodhi maa rehti thi. Unke guru, Rishi Matang, ne kaha tha, 'Ek din Shri Ram tumhare dwaar aayenge.' Isliye saalon tak, har subah, Shabari raasta saaf karti aur intezaar karti.

text.en: She scattered flowers on the path so his feet would feel soft earth. She hummed his name while she worked. Her hair turned white and her back grew bent, but her hope never grew old.
text.hinglish: Woh raaste par phool bichhaati taaki unke pairon ko narm dharti mile. Kaam karte hue unka naam gungunaati. Unke baal safed ho gaye, kamar jhuk gayi, par unki ummeed kabhi boodhi nahi hui.

text.en: One day she picked wild ber from the trees. She wanted to give Ram only the sweetest ones, so she tasted each berry first. The sour ones she kept aside; the sweet ones she saved in a little basket.
text.hinglish: Ek din usne pedon se jungli ber tode. Woh Ram ko sirf sabse meethe ber dena chahti thi, isliye har ber pehle khud chakha. Khatte alag rakh diye; meethe ek chhoti tokri mein sambhaal liye.

text.en: And then Shri Ram and Lakshman truly came! Shabari washed their feet with tears of joy and offered her tasted berries. Lakshman hesitated, but Shri Ram ate every one with a big smile. 'I have never tasted anything sweeter,' he said.
text.hinglish: Aur phir sach mein Shri Ram aur Lakshman aa gaye! Shabari ne khushi ke aansuon se unke pair dhoye aur chakhe hue ber diye. Lakshman jhijhke, par Shri Ram ne har ber muskura kar khaaya. 'Maine isse meetha kuch nahi chakha,' unhone kaha.

text.en: Shri Ram did not see an old, poor woman. He saw a heart full of love. Shabari teaches us that God and good people value love more than riches, and patience is a kind of prayer too.
text.hinglish: Shri Ram ne ek boodhi, gareeb aurat nahi dekhi. Unhone pyaar se bhara dil dekha. Shabari sikhaati hain ki Bhagwan aur achhe log dhan se zyada pyaar ko maante hain, aur dheeraj bhi ek prarthana hai.

say.en: Little one, I am waiting for you with the sweetest love, like Shabari waited.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, main tumhara intezaar sabse meethe pyaar se kar rahi hoon, jaise Shabari ne kiya.

moral.en: Love and patience are the sweetest offerings.
moral.hinglish: Pyaar aur dheeraj sabse meethi bhent hain.

reflection.en: What are you lovingly preparing for your baby's arrival?
reflection.hinglish: Baby ke aane ke liye aap pyaar se kya taiyaari kar rahi hain?

q.en: Shabari tasted the berries to find the sweetest ones.
q.hinglish: Shabari ne sabse meethe ber dhoondhne ke liye chakhe.

q.en: Shri Ram refused the berries.
q.hinglish: Shri Ram ne ber khaane se mana kar diya.

q.en: Shabari waited for many years.
q.hinglish: Shabari ne kai saal intezaar kiya.

title.en: Young Bharat and the lion cub
title.hinglish: Nanha Bharat aur sher ka bachcha

text.en: In the peaceful ashram of Rishi Kanva lived Shakuntala and her little son. The deer ate from his hands, peacocks danced for him, and he was not afraid of anything in the forest.
text.hinglish: Rishi Kanva ke shaant ashram mein Shakuntala aur unka nanha beta rehte the. Hiran uske haathon se khaate, mor uske liye naachte, aur use jungle mein kisi cheez se dar nahi lagta tha.

text.en: One day King Dushyanta, riding through the forest, saw an amazing sight: a small boy holding open a lion cub's mouth, laughing. 'Open wide!' the boy said. 'I want to count your teeth!'
text.hinglish: Ek din Raja Dushyant jungle se guzar rahe the aur unhone adbhut nazaara dekha: ek chhota ladka sher ke bachche ka munh khole hans raha tha. 'Bada sa kholo!' ladka bola. 'Mujhe tumhare daant ginne hain!'

text.en: The king was amazed. 'Who is this fearless child?' The boy was gentle with the cub, and even the mother lioness watched calmly. Courage and kindness lived together in his small heart.
text.hinglish: Raja hairaan reh gaye. 'Yeh nidar baalak kaun hai?' Ladka bachche ke saath komal tha, aur sherni bhi shaanti se dekh rahi thi. Uske nanhe dil mein himmat aur dayaa saath-saath rehti thi.

question.en: If you met such a brave child, what would you tell him?
question.hinglish: Aise bahadur baalak se milein to aap kya kahengi?

label.en: Be brave, and always be gentle
label.hinglish: Bahadur raho, aur hamesha komal raho

lesson.en: Beautiful! True courage never hurts the weak.
lesson.hinglish: Sundar! Sachchi himmat kamzor ko kabhi chot nahi pahunchaati.

label.en: Ask him how he became so fearless
label.hinglish: Poochhein woh itna nidar kaise bana

lesson.en: He would say: love. Animals trust those who are kind to them.
lesson.hinglish: Woh kahega: pyaar se. Jaanwar dayaalu logon par bharosa karte hain.

text.en: Dushyanta learned that this was his own son with Shakuntala. With great joy he took them home. The boy, Bharat, grew up to be a wise and fair king who cared for every person in his land.
text.hinglish: Dushyant ko pata chala ki yeh Shakuntala se unka apna beta hai. Bahut khushi se woh unhe ghar le gaye. Baalak Bharat bada hokar ek samajhdaar aur nyaayi raja bana jo apne raajya ke har insaan ki parwaah karta tha.

text.en: Here is the wonderful part: our country is called Bharat after him! Every time we say 'Bharat Mata', we remember a little boy who was brave, kind and fair.
text.hinglish: Aur sabse pyaari baat: hamara desh unhi ke naam par Bharat kehlaata hai! Jab bhi hum 'Bharat Mata' kehte hain, hum ek nanhe baalak ko yaad karte hain jo bahadur, dayaalu aur nyaayi tha.

say.en: Little one, you are a child of Bharat. Be brave and kind.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum Bharat ki santaan ho. Bahadur aur dayaalu bano.

moral.en: Real courage walks hand in hand with kindness.
moral.hinglish: Asli himmat dayaa ke saath chalti hai.

reflection.en: Which quality would you most like your child to have: courage, kindness or fairness?
reflection.hinglish: Aap chahengi bachche mein sabse zyada kaun sa gun ho: himmat, dayaa ya nyaay?

q.en: Little Bharat counted a lion cub's teeth.
q.hinglish: Nanhe Bharat ne sher ke bachche ke daant gine.

q.en: Our country Bharat is named after him.
q.hinglish: Hamara desh Bharat unke naam par hai.

q.en: Bharat was cruel to animals.
q.hinglish: Bharat jaanwaron ke saath kroor tha.

text.en: Long ago lived a curious boy named Nachiketa. His father was giving gifts at a great yagna, but he was giving away only old, tired cows. Nachiketa felt this was not right. A gift should be given with an open heart.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle Nachiketa naam ka ek jigyaasu baalak tha. Uske pita ek bade yagya mein daan de rahe the, par sirf boodhi, thaki gaayein de rahe the. Nachiketa ko yeh theek nahi laga. Daan khule dil se dena chahiye.

text.en: 'Father,' he asked politely, 'to whom will you give me?' He asked again and again. His father, upset, said, 'To Yama!' Yama is the wise lord of life's ending. Nachiketa took the words seriously and set out to meet him.
text.hinglish: 'Pitaji,' usne vinamrata se poochha, 'mujhe kise daan denge?' Usne baar-baar poochha. Pita ne pareshaan hokar kaha, 'Yamraj ko!' Yamraj jeevan ke ant ke gyaani devta hain. Nachiketa ne baat ko gambheerta se liya aur unse milne chal pada.

text.en: Yama was away, so Nachiketa waited at his door for three days, calmly, without food. When Yama returned, he was touched. 'You waited so patiently. I will give you three wishes.'
text.hinglish: Yamraj ghar par nahi the, to Nachiketa teen din tak unke dwaar par shaanti se, bina khaaye, intezaar karta raha. Lautne par Yamraj bahut prabhaavit hue. 'Tumne itne dheeraj se intezaar kiya. Main tumhe teen var doonga.'

text.en: First Nachiketa wished for his father's peace of mind. Second, to learn a sacred fire ritual. For the third, Yama offered gold, kingdoms and long life. But Nachiketa said, 'Teach me what lasts forever.'
text.hinglish: Pehle var mein Nachiketa ne pita ke mann ki shaanti maangi. Doosre mein ek pavitra agni vidya. Teesre ke liye Yamraj ne sona, raajya aur lambi umar dene chaahi. Par Nachiketa bola, 'Mujhe woh sikhaaiye jo hamesha rehta hai.'

text.en: Yama smiled and taught him that the true self, the atma, is never born and never ends. This conversation is in the Katha Upanishad. A small boy's honest question became wisdom for all of us.
text.hinglish: Yamraj muskuraaye aur sikhaaya ki asli 'main', yaani aatma, na janm leti hai na khatam hoti hai. Yeh baatcheet Katha Upanishad mein hai. Ek nanhe baalak ka sachcha sawaal hum sabke liye gyaan ban gaya.

say.en: Little one, ask your questions bravely. I will always listen.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, apne sawaal himmat se poochhna. Main hamesha sunoongi.

moral.en: Honest questions, patience and wanting what truly lasts lead to wisdom.
moral.hinglish: Sachche sawaal, dheeraj aur sthaayi cheez ki chaah gyaan tak le jaate hain.

reflection.en: What is something that truly lasts that you want to give your child?
reflection.hinglish: Aap bachche ko aisi kaun si cheez dena chahengi jo hamesha rahe?

q.en: Nachiketa waited three days at Yama's door.
q.hinglish: Nachiketa ne teen din Yamraj ke dwaar par intezaar kiya.

q.en: For his third wish, Nachiketa chose gold.
q.hinglish: Teesre var mein Nachiketa ne sona chuna.

q.en: This story is in the Katha Upanishad.
q.hinglish: Yeh kahani Katha Upanishad mein hai.

title.hinglish: Ganesh ji ki duniya ki parikrama

text.en: One day Narad Muni brought a special fruit to Kailash, the fruit of wisdom. Shiva and Parvati had two sons, Kartikeya and Ganesha, and both wanted it. 'Let's have a race,' said Shiva. 'Whoever goes around the whole world first gets the fruit.'
text.hinglish: Ek din Narad Muni Kailash par ek khaas phal laaye, gyaan ka phal. Shiv ji aur Parvati ji ke do bete the, Kartikeya aur Ganesh, aur dono ko woh chahiye tha. 'Daud lagaate hain,' Shiv ji bole. 'Jo pehle poori duniya ka chakkar lagaayega, use phal milega.'

text.en: Kartikeya jumped onto his swift peacock and zoomed away over mountains, rivers and oceans. Ganesha looked at his ride, a tiny mouse, and smiled. He didn't worry. He thought.
text.hinglish: Kartikeya apne tez mor par baithe aur pahaadon, nadiyon aur samudron ke upar ud gaye. Ganesh ji ne apni sawaari, ek nanhe chooha, ko dekha aur muskuraaye. Woh ghabraaye nahi. Unhone socha.

question.en: Ganesha's ride is a slow little mouse. What can he do?
question.hinglish: Ganesh ji ki sawaari ek dheema chooha hai. Woh kya kar sakte hain?

label.en: Think calmly about what 'the world' means
label.hinglish: Shaanti se sochein 'duniya' ka matlab kya hai

lesson.en: That's what he did! A calm mind finds clever answers.
lesson.hinglish: Unhone yahi kiya! Shaant mann chatur jawaab dhoondhta hai.

label.en: Try his best anyway, without giving up
label.hinglish: Phir bhi poori koshish karein, haar na maanein

lesson.en: A good spirit! And with a little thinking, his best became brilliant.
lesson.hinglish: Achhi soch! Aur thoda sochne se unka best shaandaar ban gaya.

text.en: Ganesha folded his hands and walked slowly, lovingly, three times around his parents, Shiva and Parvati. Then he bowed. 'My parents are my whole world,' he said. 'I have gone around the world.'
text.hinglish: Ganesh ji ne haath jode aur dheere-dheere, pyaar se, apne maata-pita Shiv aur Parvati ke teen chakkar lagaaye. Phir pranaam kiya. 'Mere maata-pita hi meri poori duniya hain,' unhone kaha. 'Maine duniya ka chakkar laga liya.'

text.en: Shiva and Parvati were deeply moved, and gave him the fruit. When Kartikeya returned, tired and dusty, he understood, and he loved his brother all the more. The brothers hugged and shared the joy.
text.hinglish: Shiv ji aur Parvati ji bahut bhaavuk hue, aur phal unhe de diya. Jab Kartikeya thake aur dhool bhare lautay, to woh samajh gaye, aur bhai se aur bhi pyaar karne lage. Dono bhaiyon ne gale milkar khushi baanti.

text.en: That is why we pray to Ganesha first before anything new: for his wisdom. And this story reminds every child that a family's love is a whole world.
text.hinglish: Isiliye har naye kaam se pehle hum Ganesh ji ki puja karte hain: unki buddhi ke liye. Aur yeh kahani har bachche ko yaad dilaati hai ki parivaar ka pyaar ek poori duniya hai.

say.en: Little one, you are already my whole world.
say.hinglish: Mere laado/laadle, tum abhi se meri poori duniya ho.

moral.en: Wisdom often means seeing what truly matters, and family love is a whole world.
moral.hinglish: Buddhi aksar yeh dekhna hai ki asli maayne kya rakhta hai, aur parivaar ka pyaar poori duniya hai.

reflection.en: Who has been your whole world, and how can you thank them this week?
reflection.hinglish: Aapki poori duniya kaun raha hai, aur is hafte aap unhe kaise shukriya kahengi?

q.en: Ganesha's ride is a mouse.
q.hinglish: Ganesh ji ki sawaari chooha hai.

q.en: Ganesha flew around all the oceans.
q.hinglish: Ganesh ji saare samudron ke upar ude.

q.en: Ganesha went around his parents three times.
q.hinglish: Ganesh ji ne maata-pita ke teen chakkar lagaaye.

text.en: When they were boys, Krishna and Sudama studied together at Guru Sandipani's ashram. They fetched firewood, shared food and laughed together. Krishna became a king of Dwarka; Sudama stayed a poor, honest teacher.
text.hinglish: Bachpan mein Krishna aur Sudama Guru Sandipani ke ashram mein saath padhte the. Saath lakdi laate, khaana baant-te aur hanste. Krishna Dwarka ke raja bane; Sudama ek gareeb, imaandaar shikshak hi rahe.

text.en: Years later, Sudama's family had very little to eat. His wife said, 'Go and meet your friend Krishna.' Sudama felt shy. 'What gift can I take to a king?' He tied a handful of beaten rice, poha, in an old cloth.
text.hinglish: Saalon baad Sudama ke ghar khaane ko bahut kam tha. Patni ne kaha, 'Apne mitra Krishna se milkar aaiye.' Sudama jhijhke. 'Raja ke liye kya bhent le jaaoon?' Unhone ek purane kapde mein mutthi bhar poha baandh liya.

text.en: At the palace, the guards looked at his torn clothes. But when Krishna heard 'Sudama', he ran out barefoot, hugged him, washed his tired feet and sat him on his own throne!
text.hinglish: Mahal mein pehredaaron ne uske phate kapde dekhe. Par jaise hi Krishna ne 'Sudama' suna, woh nange pair daude aaye, gale lagaaya, thake pair dhoye aur unhe apne singhaasan par bitha diya!

text.en: Sudama hid his little bundle, embarrassed. Krishna found it, laughing. 'Poha! My favourite!' He ate it happily, as if it were the finest feast. Sudama was too shy to ask for any help, and Krishna asked him nothing.
text.hinglish: Sudama ne sharmaakar apni potli chhupa li. Krishna ne hanste hue dhoondh li. 'Poha! Mera pasandida!' Unhone use khushi se khaaya, jaise sabse badhiya daawat ho. Sudama madad maangne mein sharmaa gaye, aur Krishna ne kuch nahi poochha.

text.en: When Sudama walked home, his hut had become a beautiful house, and his family was smiling. Krishna had understood without a single word. True friends see your heart, not your clothes.
text.hinglish: Jab Sudama ghar laute, unki jhopdi ek sundar ghar ban gayi thi, aur parivaar muskura raha tha. Krishna bina ek shabd ke samajh gaye the. Sachche dost kapde nahi, dil dekhte hain.

say.en: Little one, may you always have true friends, and be one too.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tumhe hamesha sachche dost milein, aur tum bhi sachche dost bano.

moral.en: True friendship sees the heart, and a small gift given with love is precious.
moral.hinglish: Sachchi dosti dil dekhti hai, aur pyaar se diya chhota tohfa anmol hai.

reflection.en: Who is your Sudama, the friend who loves you as you are?
reflection.hinglish: Aapka Sudama kaun hai, jo aapko jaisi hain waisi pasand karta hai?

q.en: Krishna and Sudama studied together as boys.
q.hinglish: Krishna aur Sudama bachpan mein saath padhe.

q.en: Sudama brought gold for Krishna.
q.hinglish: Sudama Krishna ke liye sona laaye.

q.en: Krishna ate the poha happily.
q.hinglish: Krishna ne poha khushi se khaaya.

text.en: Long ago a baby was born whose body was bent in eight places, so he was called Ashtavakra, 'eight bends'. His body was different, but his mind was bright as a lamp. He loved to learn and listened to every lesson with care.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle ek baalak paida hua jiska sharir aath jagah se muda tha, isliye naam pada Ashtavakra, 'aath mod'. Uska sharir alag tha, par mann deepak jaisa ujjwal. Use seekhna pasand tha aur woh har paath dhyaan se sunta.

text.en: When he was only twelve, he went to King Janaka's court in Mithila, where great scholars debated. As he walked in, some of them laughed at the way he moved.
text.hinglish: Jab woh sirf baarah saal ka tha, Mithila mein Raja Janak ke darbaar gaya, jahan bade vidvaan shaastrarth karte the. Jaise hi woh andar aaya, kuch log uske chalne ke dhang par hans pade.

text.en: Ashtavakra laughed too. 'I thought this was a court of wise people,' he said calmly. 'But you are looking only at my skin and bones, like a leather-seller judges hides. The wise look at the spirit.'
text.hinglish: Ashtavakra bhi hans pada. 'Maine socha tha yeh gyaaniyon ka darbaar hai,' usne shaanti se kaha. 'Par aap sirf meri tvacha aur haddi dekh rahe hain, jaise chamde ka vyapaari khaal parakhta hai. Gyaani aatma dekhte hain.'

question.en: People laugh at Ashtavakra. What is the best answer?
question.hinglish: Log Ashtavakra par hanste hain. Sabse achha jawaab kya hai?

label.en: Stay calm and speak wisely
label.hinglish: Shaant rehkar samajhdaari se bole

lesson.en: That's what he did, and the room fell silent with respect.
lesson.hinglish: Usne yahi kiya, aur poora darbaar aadar se chup ho gaya.

label.en: Let his knowledge speak for itself
label.hinglish: Apne gyaan ko bolne de
