lesson.en: Yes! He went on to win the debate and everyone learned from him.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Usne shaastrarth jeeta aur sabne usse seekha.

text.en: The court went quiet. King Janaka bowed to the boy. Ashtavakra answered the hardest questions with such clarity that he won the great debate, and the king became his student.
text.hinglish: Darbaar shaant ho gaya. Raja Janak ne baalak ko pranaam kiya. Ashtavakra ne sabse kathin sawaalon ke itne saaf jawaab diye ki usne bada shaastrarth jeet liya, aur raja uske shishya ban gaye.

text.en: Their talks became the Ashtavakra Gita, about peace and freedom inside. Ashtavakra teaches us never to judge anyone by how they look, and to love every body, including our own.
text.hinglish: Unki baatein Ashtavakra Gita bani, man ki shaanti aur aazaadi ke baare mein. Ashtavakra sikhaate hain ki kisi ko roop se kabhi mat aanko, aur har sharir se pyaar karo, apne se bhi.

say.en: Little one, however you are, you are perfect to us.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum jaise bhi ho, hamare liye poore ho.

moral.en: Never judge anyone by how they look; wisdom lives inside.
moral.hinglish: Kisi ko roop se mat aanko; gyaan andar rehta hai.

reflection.en: How can your family teach your child to respect everyone?
reflection.hinglish: Aapka parivaar bachche ko sabka aadar karna kaise sikhaayega?

q.en: Ashtavakra means 'eight bends'.
q.hinglish: Ashtavakra ka matlab hai 'aath mod'.

q.en: Ashtavakra got angry and left the court.
q.hinglish: Ashtavakra gussa hokar darbaar chhod gaya.

q.en: King Janaka became his student.
q.hinglish: Raja Janak uske shishya bane.

text.en: In ancient times lived a brilliant scholar named Gargi Vachaknavi. She studied the Vedas, thought deeply about the stars, the sky and the soul, and was known across the land for her sharp mind.
text.hinglish: Praacheen kaal mein Gargi Vachaknavi naam ki ek mahaan vidushi thi. Usne Vedon ka adhyayan kiya, taaron, aasmaan aur aatma par gehraai se socha, aur apni tez buddhi ke liye poore desh mein jaani jaati thi.

text.en: King Janaka held a great gathering of scholars and offered a thousand cows with gold on their horns to the wisest person. The sage Yajnavalkya calmly said, 'I will take them,' and many scholars challenged him.
text.hinglish: Raja Janak ne vidvaanon ki badi sabha bulaayi aur sabse gyaani ko sone se saje seengon wali hazaar gaayein dene ki ghoshna ki. Rishi Yajnavalkya ne shaanti se kaha, 'Main le loonga,' aur kai vidvaanon ne unhe chunauti di.

text.en: Then Gargi stood up, the only woman to speak in that great hall. 'Everything is woven in water,' she asked, 'but in what is water woven? And that in what?' Question after question, deeper and deeper, like climbing to the sky.
text.hinglish: Tab Gargi khadi hui, us bade sabha-bhavan mein bolne wali akeli mahila. 'Sab kuch paani mein buna hai,' usne poochha, 'par paani kismein buna hai? Aur woh kismein?' Sawaal ke baad sawaal, gehre aur gehre, jaise aasmaan tak seedhi.

text.en: Yajnavalkya answered with respect, and Gargi listened carefully. At the end she told the gathering, 'He is truly wise. No one can defeat him in this.' She was honest enough to praise him.
text.hinglish: Yajnavalkya ne aadar se jawaab diye, aur Gargi ne dhyaan se suna. Ant mein usne sabha se kaha, 'Yeh sach mein gyaani hain. Is vishay mein inhe koi nahi haraa sakta.' Woh itni imaandaar thi ki usne unki taareef ki.

text.en: Their conversation is in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. Gargi shows us that a curious mind is beautiful, that every child's questions deserve answers, and that being honest is part of being wise.
text.hinglish: Unki baatcheet Brihadaranyaka Upanishad mein hai. Gargi dikhaati hai ki jigyaasu mann sundar hai, har bachche ke sawaal jawaab ke haqdaar hain, aur imaandaari bhi gyaan ka hissa hai.

say.en: Little one, keep asking 'why'. Your questions are welcome in our home.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, 'kyon' poochhte rehna. Hamare ghar mein tumhare sawaalon ka swagat hai.

moral.en: A curious, honest mind is a treasure, and every question deserves respect.
moral.hinglish: Jigyaasu aur imaandaar mann ek khazaana hai, aur har sawaal aadar ka haqdaar hai.

reflection.en: What questions did you love asking as a child?
reflection.hinglish: Bachpan mein aapko kaun se sawaal poochhna pasand tha?

q.en: Gargi questioned the sage Yajnavalkya.
q.hinglish: Gargi ne Rishi Yajnavalkya se sawaal poochhe.

q.en: Gargi refused to praise anyone.
q.hinglish: Gargi ne kisi ki taareef nahi ki.

q.en: The gathering was held by King Janaka.
q.hinglish: Sabha Raja Janak ne bulaayi thi.

text.en: Every year the people of Vrindavan prayed to Indra, the king of rain, with big feasts. Little Krishna asked, 'Why? It is Govardhan hill that gives our cows grass, our streams water and our village shade. Let's thank Govardhan!'
text.hinglish: Har saal Vrindavan ke log baarish ke raja Indra ki badi daawat se puja karte the. Nanhe Krishna ne poochha, 'Kyon? Govardhan parvat hi hamari gaayon ko ghaas, nadiyon ko paani aur gaon ko chhaanv deta hai. Chalo Govardhan ka shukriya karein!'

text.en: So the villagers thanked the hill instead. Indra felt proud and hurt. He sent black clouds, roaring thunder and pouring rain. The rain fell and fell. The cows mooed in fear and the children held their mothers tight.
text.hinglish: To gaon walon ne parvat ka shukriya kiya. Indra ka ahankaar aahat hua. Unhone kaale baadal, garajti bijli aur moosladhaar baarish bheji. Baarish girti rahi, girti rahi. Gaayein dar se rambhaayi aur bachche maaon se lipat gaye.

text.en: Krishna smiled calmly. He walked to Govardhan hill and lifted the whole mountain on the tip of his little finger, like a giant umbrella! 'Come, everyone, come underneath with your cows!'
text.hinglish: Krishna shaanti se muskuraaye. Woh Govardhan parvat tak gaye aur poore pahaad ko apni chhoti ungli ki nok par utha liya, jaise ek vishaal chhaata! 'Aao, sab log, apni gaayon ke saath neeche aa jaao!'

text.en: For seven days and nights the whole village stayed safe and dry under the hill, singing and sharing food. At last Indra understood his pride, stopped the rain and bowed to Krishna. The sun came out.
text.hinglish: Saat din aur saat raat poora gaon parvat ke neeche surakshit aur sookha raha, gaate aur khaana baant-te hue. Aakhir Indra ko apna ahankaar samajh aaya, baarish rok di aur Krishna ko pranaam kiya. Dhoop nikal aayi.

text.en: That is why, the day after Diwali, families make a little Govardhan from food or cow dung and celebrate Annakoot. We thank the earth that feeds us, and remember that love protects everyone together.
text.hinglish: Isiliye Diwali ke agle din parivaar khaane ya gobar se chhota Govardhan banaate hain aur Annakoot manaate hain. Hum us dharti ka shukriya karte hain jo hume khilaati hai, aur yaad rakhte hain ki pyaar sabki saath raksha karta hai.

say.en: Little one, we will always hold an umbrella of love over you.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, hum hamesha tumhare upar pyaar ka chhaata rakhenge.

moral.en: Be thankful to nature, and protect each other together.
moral.hinglish: Prakriti ka shukriya karo, aur milkar ek-doosre ki raksha karo.

reflection.en: What in nature are you most thankful for today?
reflection.hinglish: Aaj aap prakriti ki kis cheez ke liye sabse zyada shukraguzaar hain?

q.en: Krishna lifted Govardhan on his little finger.
q.hinglish: Krishna ne Govardhan chhoti ungli par uthaaya.

q.en: The rain lasted for one hour.
q.hinglish: Baarish ek ghante chali.

q.en: Govardhan Puja is celebrated after Diwali.
q.hinglish: Govardhan Puja Diwali ke baad hoti hai.

text.en: Long ago the land was dry and the people's hearts were heavy. A king named Bhagirath wished to bring the holy river Ganga down from the heavens, so the earth could be green and his ancestors could find peace.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle dharti sookhi thi aur logon ke mann bhaari the. Raja Bhagirath chahte the ki pavitra Ganga swarg se dharti par utrein, taaki dharti hari ho aur unke purvajon ko shaanti mile.

text.en: Bhagirath left his palace and prayed for years, through summer heat and winter snow. When Ganga finally agreed, she warned, 'My waters are so mighty, the earth will crack if I fall on it.'
text.hinglish: Bhagirath mahal chhodkar saalon tak tapasya karte rahe, garmi ki dhoop aur sardi ki barf mein. Jab Ganga maan gayi, to unhone chetaaya, 'Meri dhaara itni tez hai ki main giri to dharti phat jaayegi.'

text.en: Bhagirath did not give up. He prayed again, this time to Lord Shiva. Shiva agreed to help, and stood ready on the Himalayas with his long hair spread wide.
text.hinglish: Bhagirath ne haar nahi maani. Unhone phir prarthana ki, is baar Bhagwan Shiv se. Shiv ji madad ko maan gaye, aur apni lambi jataayein phailaakar Himalaya par khade ho gaye.

question.en: One problem was solved and a new one appeared. What should Bhagirath do?
question.hinglish: Ek mushkil suljhi aur nayi aa gayi. Bhagirath ko kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Keep going, step by step
label.hinglish: Kadam-dar-kadam chalte rahein

lesson.en: Yes! Big dreams are reached one step at a time.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Bade sapne ek-ek kadam se poore hote hain.

label.en: Ask for help from someone wiser
label.hinglish: Kisi samajhdaar se madad maangein

lesson.en: Exactly what he did. Asking Shiva for help was the key.
lesson.hinglish: Bilkul yahi kiya. Shiv ji se madad maangna hi kunji thi.

text.en: Ganga rushed down from the sky, roaring, and Shiva caught her softly in his locks. Then he let her flow gently out, in streams, onto the mountains. The wild river became a calm, life-giving one.
text.hinglish: Ganga garajte hue aasmaan se utri, aur Shiv ji ne unhe apni jataon mein komalta se thaam liya. Phir dheere-dheere dhaaraon mein pahaadon par baha diya. Tez nadi ek shaant, jeevan dene wali nadi ban gayi.

text.en: Bhagirath walked ahead and Ganga followed him across the plains, turning brown fields green. Even today, when someone works patiently and never gives up, we call it 'Bhagirath prayatna'.
text.hinglish: Bhagirath aage chale aur Ganga unke peeche maidaanon mein bahi, bhoore khet hare ho gaye. Aaj bhi jab koi dheeraj se mehnat kare aur haar na maane, to use 'Bhagirath prayatna' kehte hain.

say.en: Little one, keep trying, keep flowing, like Ganga.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, koshish karte raho, Ganga jaise behte raho.

moral.en: Patient, steady effort can bring even a river from the sky.
moral.hinglish: Dheeraj aur lagaataar mehnat aasmaan se nadi bhi la sakti hai.

reflection.en: What is your 'Bhagirath prayatna', something you keep working towards?
reflection.hinglish: Aapka 'Bhagirath prayatna' kya hai, jiske liye aap lagaataar mehnat kar rahi hain?

q.en: Shiva caught Ganga in his hair.
q.hinglish: Shiv ji ne Ganga ko jataon mein thaama.

q.en: Bhagirath gave up after one try.
q.hinglish: Bhagirath ne ek koshish ke baad haar maan li.

q.en: 'Bhagirath prayatna' means great, patient effort.
q.hinglish: 'Bhagirath prayatna' yaani bada, dheeraj bhara prayaas.

text.en: Long ago, in the palace garden of Kapilavastu, young Prince Siddhartha loved to sit quietly under the trees, watching birds fly across the blue sky. He felt that every living thing wanted to be happy, just like him.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle Kapilvastu ke mahal ke baag mein yuva Rajkumar Siddharth pedon ke neeche shaanti se baithkar neele aasmaan mein udti chidiyan dekhna pasand karte the. Unhe lagta tha ki har jeev, unki tarah, khush rehna chahta hai.

text.en: One day a beautiful white swan fell from the sky, an arrow in its wing. Siddhartha ran to it, gently pulled out the arrow, put healing herbs on the wound and held the frightened bird close.
text.hinglish: Ek din ek sundar safed hans aasmaan se gira, uske pankh mein teer laga tha. Siddharth daud kar gaye, dheere se teer nikaala, ghaav par jadi-booti lagaayi aur dare hue pakshi ko seene se lagaaya.

text.en: His cousin Devadatta came running. 'That's my swan! I shot it. Give it to me.' Siddhartha held the swan softly. 'You tried to take its life. I am trying to save it. It should go to the one who protects it.'
text.hinglish: Unka chachera bhai Devadatt daudta aaya. 'Woh mera hans hai! Maine maara. Mujhe do.' Siddharth ne hans ko komalta se thaama. 'Tumne iski jaan lene ki koshish ki. Main ise bachaa raha hoon. Yeh bachaane wale ka hona chahiye.'

text.en: They went to the king's court. A wise man said, 'Life belongs to the one who saves it, not the one who harms it.' The swan was given to Siddhartha, who cared for it until it could fly again.
text.hinglish: Dono raaj-darbaar gaye. Ek gyaani ne kaha, 'Jeevan bachaane wale ka hota hai, chot pahunchaane wale ka nahi.' Hans Siddharth ko mila, aur unhone tab tak uski dekhbhaal ki jab tak woh phir se udne laayak na ho gaya.

text.en: Siddhartha grew up to become the Buddha, who taught the world kindness to all beings. It began with a small, gentle act for one wounded bird.
text.hinglish: Siddharth bade hokar Buddh bane, jinhone duniya ko har jeev ke prati karuna sikhaayi. Iski shuruaat ek ghaayal pakshi ke liye ek chhote, komal kaam se hui thi.

say.en: Little one, be gentle with every living thing.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, har jeev ke saath komal rehna.

moral.en: Kindness to all living beings is true strength.
moral.hinglish: Har jeev ke prati dayaa hi asli shakti hai.

reflection.en: How will you teach your child to care for animals and birds?
reflection.hinglish: Aap bachche ko jaanwaron aur pakshiyon ki parwaah karna kaise sikhaayengi?

q.en: Siddhartha saved a wounded swan.
q.hinglish: Siddharth ne ghaayal hans bachaaya.

q.en: The court gave the swan to Devadatta.
q.hinglish: Darbaar ne hans Devadatt ko diya.

q.en: Siddhartha later became the Buddha.
q.hinglish: Siddharth baad mein Buddh bane.

title.hinglish: Hanuman ko yaad aayi apni shakti

text.en: The vanar sena reached the edge of the great ocean, searching for Sita. Lanka was far across the water. 'Who can jump so far?' they wondered. One said ten yojanas, another said twenty. No one could go all the way.
text.hinglish: Vanar sena Sita ji ko dhoondhte hue mahasaagar ke kinaare pahunchi. Lanka paani ke us paar bahut door thi. 'Itni door kaun koodega?' sab sochne lage. Kisi ne kaha dus yojan, kisi ne bees. Poora koi nahi ja sakta tha.

text.en: Hanuman sat quietly at the back. As a child he had been so playful that a sage's blessing made him forget his powers until someone reminded him. So he did not know how strong he really was.
text.hinglish: Hanuman ji peeche chupchaap baithe the. Bachpan mein woh itne natkhat the ki ek rishi ke aashirvaad se woh apni shakti bhool gaye the, jab tak koi yaad na dilaaye. Isliye unhe pata hi nahi tha woh kitne shaktishaali hain.

text.en: Then wise old Jambavan, the bear king, walked up to him. 'Hanuman, why are you silent? You are the son of the wind! You once leapt for the sun. Remember who you are!'
text.hinglish: Tab gyaani, boodhe reechh-raja Jambavan unke paas aaye. 'Hanuman, tum chup kyon ho? Tum pawan-putra ho! Tumne ek baar suraj tak chhalaang lagaayi thi. Yaad karo tum kaun ho!'

text.en: As Jambavan spoke, Hanuman began to grow, taller and taller, glowing with confidence. He climbed Mount Mahendra, said 'Jai Shri Ram', and leapt across the ocean in one great jump to Lanka.
text.hinglish: Jambavan bolte gaye aur Hanuman ji badhne lage, aur unche, aatmavishvaas se chamakte hue. Woh Mahendra parvat par chadhe, 'Jai Shri Ram' kaha, aur ek vishaal chhalaang mein samudra paar karke Lanka pahunch gaye.

text.en: Sometimes we all forget how strong we are. A loving voice that says 'you can do it' is a precious gift. Be a Jambavan for the people you love.
text.hinglish: Kabhi-kabhi hum sab bhool jaate hain ki hum kitne majboot hain. Ek pyaari awaaz jo kahe 'tum kar sakte ho', anmol tohfa hai. Apne pyaaron ke liye Jambavan baniye.

say.en: Little one, you are stronger than you know. I will always remind you.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum apni soch se zyada majboot ho. Main hamesha yaad dilaaungi.

moral.en: Encouragement can awaken the strength already inside us.
moral.hinglish: Hausla badhaane se andar chhupi shakti jaag uthti hai.

reflection.en: Who reminded you of your strength when you needed it?
reflection.hinglish: Zaroorat padne par kisne aapko aapki shakti yaad dilaayi?

q.en: Jambavan reminded Hanuman of his strength.
q.hinglish: Jambavan ne Hanuman ko unki shakti yaad dilaayi.

q.en: Hanuman swam across the ocean slowly.
q.hinglish: Hanuman dheere-dheere tairkar samudra paar gaye.

q.en: Jambavan is a bear king.
q.hinglish: Jambavan reechh-raja hain.

text.en: Guru Dronacharya was teaching archery to the young princes. One day he placed a small wooden bird high on a tree branch. 'Today's test,' he said. 'You must hit the bird's eye.'
text.hinglish: Guru Dronacharya rajkumaron ko dhanurvidya sikha rahe the. Ek din unhone pedh ki oonchi daal par lakdi ki ek chhoti chidiya rakhi. 'Aaj ki pareeksha,' unhone kaha. 'Chidiya ki aankh par nishaana lagaana hai.'

text.en: He called Yudhishthira first. 'Take aim. What do you see?' 'I see the tree, the branches, the leaves, the bird, my brothers and you, Guruji.' Drona said gently, 'Put down your bow.'
text.hinglish: Unhone pehle Yudhishthir ko bulaaya. 'Nishaana saadho. Kya dikh raha hai?' 'Mujhe ped, daalein, patte, chidiya, mere bhai aur aap dikh rahe hain, Guruji.' Drona ne pyaar se kaha, 'Dhanush neeche rakh do.'

text.en: One by one, the others said much the same: the sky, the leaves, the bird. Then came Arjuna. 'What do you see?' 'Only the eye of the bird, Guruji.' 'Not the branch? Not the bird?' 'Only the eye.'
text.hinglish: Ek-ek karke baakiyon ne bhi yahi kaha: aasmaan, patte, chidiya. Phir Arjun aaye. 'Kya dikh raha hai?' 'Sirf chidiya ki aankh, Guruji.' 'Daal nahi? Chidiya nahi?' 'Sirf aankh.'

text.en: 'Shoot,' said Drona. Arjuna's arrow flew straight into the bird's eye. Drona smiled proudly. 'When your mind is fixed on your goal, nothing else can distract you.'
text.hinglish: 'Chalaao,' Drona bole. Arjun ka teer seedha chidiya ki aankh mein laga. Drona garv se muskuraaye. 'Jab mann lakshya par tika ho, to aur kuch dhyaan nahi bhatka sakta.'

text.en: Focus is like a gentle lamp in a still room: its light goes exactly where you need it. When you breathe calmly and do one thing at a time, you are doing what Arjuna did.
text.hinglish: Dhyaan ek shaant kamre mein jalte diye jaisa hai: roshni wahin jaati hai jahan zaroorat ho. Jab aap shaanti se saans lekar ek baar mein ek kaam karti hain, to aap Arjun jaisa hi kar rahi hain.

say.en: Little one, one breath, one step, one thing at a time.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, ek saans, ek kadam, ek baar mein ek kaam.

moral.en: A focused mind reaches its goal.
moral.hinglish: Ekaagr mann apne lakshya tak pahunchta hai.

reflection.en: What helps you focus when life feels busy?
reflection.hinglish: Jab zindagi vyast lage, to dhyaan lagaane mein aapko kya madad karta hai?

q.en: Arjuna saw only the bird's eye.
q.hinglish: Arjun ko sirf chidiya ki aankh dikhi.

q.en: Yudhishthira saw only the eye too.
q.hinglish: Yudhishthir ko bhi sirf aankh dikhi.

q.en: Dronacharya was the princes' teacher.
q.hinglish: Dronacharya rajkumaron ke guru the.

text.en: A clever monkey lived in a jamun tree by a river. Every day a crocodile rested under the tree, and the monkey shared sweet jamuns with him. They became good friends and talked for hours.
text.hinglish: Nadi kinaare ek jamun ke ped par ek chatur bandar rehta tha. Roz ek magarmachh ped ke neeche aaraam karta, aur bandar use meethe jamun deta. Dono pakke dost ban gaye aur ghanton baatein karte.

text.en: The crocodile took jamuns home to his wife. She said, 'If the fruit is so sweet, the monkey's heart must be even sweeter. Bring me his heart!' The crocodile felt torn, but he agreed.
text.hinglish: Magarmachh jamun ghar patni ke liye le jaata. Patni boli, 'Agar phal itne meethe hain, to bandar ka dil aur bhi meetha hoga. Mujhe uska dil laakar do!' Magarmachh duvidha mein pada, par maan gaya.

text.en: 'Come to my home for dinner,' he told the monkey, and carried him on his back across the river. In the middle of the water he confessed the plan. The monkey's heart beat fast, but he kept calm.
text.hinglish: 'Mere ghar khaane par aao,' usne bandar se kaha, aur use peeth par bithaakar nadi mein le chala. Beech paani mein usne yojana bata di. Bandar ka dil tez dhadka, par usne dimaag shaant rakha.

question.en: The monkey is in danger in the middle of the river. What helps most?
question.hinglish: Bandar beech nadi mein khatre mein hai. Sabse zyada kya kaam aayega?

label.en: Stay calm and think
label.hinglish: Shaant rehkar sochna

lesson.en: Yes! Panic hides good ideas; calm finds them.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Ghabraahat achhe idea chhupa deti hai; shaanti dhoondh leti hai.

label.en: Use words wisely
label.hinglish: Shabdon ka samajhdaari se upyog

lesson.en: Right! A clever, gentle sentence saved his life.
lesson.hinglish: Sahi! Ek chatur, shaant vaakya ne uski jaan bachaayi.

text.en: 'Oh friend, why didn't you say so?' said the monkey. 'I keep my heart safe up in the jamun tree! Let's go back and get it.' The crocodile swam back, and the monkey sprang up into his tree, safe.
text.hinglish: 'Arre dost, pehle kyon nahi bataaya?' bandar bola. 'Main apna dil jamun ke ped par surakshit rakhta hoon! Chalo wapas chalkar le aate hain.' Magarmachh wapas tair aaya, aur bandar uchhal kar apne ped par surakshit pahunch gaya.

text.en: From the branch he called down, 'A heart lives inside, my friend, not in a tree. And true friends never trick each other.' The crocodile felt ashamed. The monkey's calm mind had saved him.
text.hinglish: Daal se usne pukaara, 'Dil andar rehta hai, dost, ped par nahi. Aur sachche dost ek-doosre ko dhokha nahi dete.' Magarmachh sharminda hua. Bandar ke shaant dimaag ne use bachaa liya.

say.en: Little one, when things feel scary, breathe and think. You will find a way.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, jab dar lage, saans lo aur socho. Raasta mil jaayega.

moral.en: Presence of mind in difficult moments can save the day.
moral.hinglish: Mushkil pal mein sooj-boojh din bachaa sakti hai.

reflection.en: When did staying calm help you most?
reflection.hinglish: Shaant rehne se aapko sabse zyada kab madad mili?

q.en: The monkey shared jamuns with the crocodile.
q.hinglish: Bandar ne magarmachh ko jamun diye.

q.en: The monkey really kept his heart in the tree.
q.hinglish: Bandar sach mein dil ped par rakhta tha.

q.en: The monkey stayed calm in danger.
q.hinglish: Khatre mein bandar shaant raha.

text.en: A friendly tortoise named Kambugriva lived in a lake with two geese, his best friends. They loved chatting every evening. The tortoise loved talking most of all.
text.hinglish: Ek jheel mein Kambugreev naam ka ek mila-jula kachhua rehta tha, aur do hans uske sabse achhe dost the. Teeno har shaam baatein karte. Kachhue ko baatein karna sabse zyada pasand tha.

text.en: One summer the lake began to dry up. 'We'll fly to a big lake far away,' said the geese. 'But how will you come?' The tortoise had an idea: 'Hold a stick in your beaks, and I'll hold the middle with my mouth!'
text.hinglish: Ek garmi mein jheel sookhne lagi. 'Hum udkar door ek badi jheel mein jaayenge,' hans bole. 'Par tum kaise aaoge?' Kachhue ko idea aaya: 'Tum chonch mein ek lakdi pakdo, main beech se munh mein pakad loonga!'

text.en: 'Good plan,' said the geese, 'but promise you won't open your mouth, not even once!' 'I promise,' said the tortoise. Up they flew, over fields and villages.
text.hinglish: 'Achhi yojana,' hans bole, 'par vaada karo ek baar bhi munh nahi khologe!' 'Vaada,' kachhua bola. Aur woh udte gaye, kheton aur gaon ke upar se.

text.en: Children below pointed and laughed: 'Look, the geese are carrying a tortoise!' The tortoise wanted so badly to answer. 'What's it to you?' he began, and the stick slipped from his mouth.
text.hinglish: Neeche bachche ishaara karke hanse: 'Dekho, hans kachhue ko le ja rahe hain!' Kachhue ka jawaab dene ka bahut mann hua. 'Tumhe kya?' bolna shuru kiya, aur lakdi munh se chhoot gayi.

text.en: Luckily he fell into a soft, muddy pond, safe but very embarrassed. The geese flew down, and they all laughed together. 'Next time,' said the tortoise, 'I'll listen first and talk later!'
text.hinglish: Kismat se woh ek naram, keechad bhare talaab mein gira, surakshit par bahut sharminda. Hans neeche aaye aur sab milkar hanse. 'Agli baar,' kachhua bola, 'pehle sunoonga, baad mein boloonga!'

say.en: Little one, there is a time to speak and a time to be quiet.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, bolne ka bhi samay hota hai aur chup rehne ka bhi.

moral.en: Keep your promises, and know when to stay quiet.
moral.hinglish: Vaade nibhaao, aur jaano kab chup rehna hai.

reflection.en: Is there someone in your family who always has something to say? Tell baby about them!
reflection.hinglish: Kya parivaar mein koi hai jiske paas hamesha kehne ko kuch hota hai? Baby ko unke baare mein bataaiye!

q.en: The tortoise promised not to open his mouth.
q.hinglish: Kachhue ne munh na kholne ka vaada kiya.

q.en: The geese carried the tortoise on their backs.
q.hinglish: Hans kachhue ko peeth par le gaye.

q.en: The tortoise learned to listen first.
q.hinglish: Kachhue ne pehle sunna seekha.

text.en: In a quiet forest lived four friends: a crow, a mouse, a tortoise and a deer. They were very different, but every evening they met by the lake to share news and laugh.
text.hinglish: Ek shaant jungle mein chaar dost rehte the: ek kauva, ek chooha, ek kachhua aur ek hiran. Woh bahut alag the, par har shaam jheel kinaare milkar baatein karte aur hanste.

text.en: One day the deer did not come. The crow flew high and spotted him caught in a hunter's net. 'Mouse, come quickly!' The crow carried the mouse to the deer, and the mouse nibbled through the ropes. The deer was free!
text.hinglish: Ek din hiran nahi aaya. Kauve ne oonchi udaan bharkar dekha ki woh shikaari ke jaal mein phansa hai. 'Choohe, jaldi aao!' Kauva choohe ko hiran tak le gaya, aur choohe ne rassi kutar di. Hiran aazaad!

text.en: But the slow tortoise had followed them, and now the hunter came back and caught him instead! He tied the tortoise to his stick and walked away. The friends quickly made a plan.
text.hinglish: Par dheema kachhua bhi peeche-peeche aa gaya tha, aur ab shikaari wapas aaya aur use pakad liya! Usne kachhue ko lakdi se baandha aur chal diya. Doston ne jaldi se yojana banaayi.

question.en: The tortoise is caught. What should the friends do?
question.hinglish: Kachhua pakda gaya. Doston ko kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Each use their own special skill
label.hinglish: Har koi apni khaas kaabiliyat lagaaye

lesson.en: Exactly! The deer, crow and mouse each had a part to play.
lesson.hinglish: Bilkul! Hiran, kauve aur choohe sabka apna kaam tha.

label.en: Make a plan together before acting
label.hinglish: Kaam se pehle milkar yojana banaayein

lesson.en: Wise! A calm plan made together worked perfectly.
lesson.hinglish: Samajhdaari! Milkar bani shaant yojana poori tarah kaam aayi.

text.en: The deer lay down by the path as if fast asleep, and the crow sat on him. The hunter dropped the tortoise and ran to catch the deer. Quick as a flash, the mouse nibbled the tortoise free!
text.hinglish: Hiran raaste mein aise let gaya jaise gehri neend mein ho, aur kauva uske upar baith gaya. Shikaari kachhue ko chhodkar hiran ki taraf bhaaga. Bijli ki tezi se choohe ne kachhue ki rassi kaat di!

text.en: The deer sprang up and ran, the crow flew, the tortoise slipped into the lake and the mouse hid in a hole. The hunter scratched his head. The four friends met again that evening, safe and happy.
text.hinglish: Hiran uchhal kar bhaaga, kauva uda, kachhua jheel mein sarak gaya aur chooha bil mein chhup gaya. Shikaari sir khujaata reh gaya. Chaaron dost us shaam phir mile, surakshit aur khush.

say.en: Little one, our family is a team. We will always help each other.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, hamara parivaar ek team hai. Hum hamesha ek-doosre ki madad karenge.

moral.en: Friends with different strengths are strongest together.
moral.hinglish: Alag-alag gunon wale dost milkar sabse majboot hote hain.

reflection.en: What special strength does each person in your family have?
reflection.hinglish: Aapke parivaar mein har kisi ki khaas taakat kya hai?

q.en: The mouse nibbled through the net.
q.hinglish: Choohe ne jaal kutar diya.

q.en: The friends left the tortoise behind.
q.hinglish: Doston ne kachhue ko chhod diya.

q.en: The deer pretended to be asleep.
q.hinglish: Hiran ne sone ka naatak kiya.

text.en: A hungry jackal named Chandarava wandered into a village at night looking for food. The village dogs chased him, barking loudly. In a panic, he jumped into a big tub of blue dye at the dyer's house.
text.hinglish: Chandrav naam ka ek bhookha siyaar raat ko khaane ki talaash mein gaon mein ghus aaya. Gaon ke kutte bhaunkte hue uske peeche pade. Ghabraakar woh rangrez ke ghar ke neel ke bade toob mein kood gaya.

text.en: When he climbed out, he was bright blue from nose to tail! Back in the forest, the animals had never seen such a creature. 'Who are you?' they whispered, a little afraid.
text.hinglish: Jab woh bahar nikla, naak se poonchh tak chamakdaar neela tha! Jungle mein jaanwaron ne aisa jeev kabhi nahi dekha tha. 'Tum kaun ho?' woh thoda darkar fusfusaaye.

text.en: The jackal had an idea. 'The gods have sent me to be your king!' he announced. The lion, tiger and elephant believed him and served him the best food. He sent away all the other jackals so no one would recognise him.
text.hinglish: Siyaar ko ek tarkeeb soojhi. 'Devtaon ne mujhe tumhara raja banaakar bheja hai!' usne ghoshna ki. Sher, baagh aur haathi ne maan liya aur use sabse badhiya khaana diya. Usne baaki siyaaron ko door bhej diya taaki koi pehchaan na le.

text.en: One full-moon night, a pack of jackals far away began to howl, 'Hoo-hoo-hooo!' The blue king could not help himself. He lifted his head and howled along. 'Hoo-hoo-hooo!'
text.hinglish: Ek poornima ki raat door siyaaron ka jhund 'Hoo-hoo-hooo!' karke chillaane laga. Neela raja khud ko rok nahi paaya. Usne sir uthaaya aur saath mein chillaaya. 'Hoo-hoo-hooo!'

text.en: 'He's only a jackal!' the animals laughed, and he ran away into the night. Pretending to be someone else is tiring and never lasts. Being your own true self is always the happiest way to live.
text.hinglish: 'Yeh to bas siyaar hai!' jaanwar hanse, aur woh raat mein bhaag gaya. Kisi aur hone ka naatak thakaata hai aur zyada der nahi chalta. Apne asli roop mein rehna hi sabse khushi bhara jeevan hai.

say.en: Little one, just be you. That is enough, and that is wonderful.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, bas tum jaise ho waise raho. Itna kaafi hai, aur bahut sundar hai.

moral.en: Be your true self; pretending never lasts.
moral.hinglish: Apne asli roop mein raho; dikhaava zyada der nahi tikta.

reflection.en: What do you love most about who you truly are?
reflection.hinglish: Aapko apne asli roop ki sabse pyaari baat kya lagti hai?

q.en: The jackal fell into blue dye.
q.hinglish: Siyaar neel mein gir gaya.

q.en: The jackal stayed king forever.
q.hinglish: Siyaar hamesha raja bana raha.

q.en: He howled with the other jackals.
q.hinglish: Usne baaki siyaaron ke saath hoo-hoo kiya.

text.en: One cold winter, Emperor Akbar announced, 'Whoever stands all night in the icy palace lake will get a big reward.' A poor man needed money for his family, so he agreed, and stood shivering in the water till dawn.
text.hinglish: Ek kadaake ki sardi mein Badshah Akbar ne ghoshna ki, 'Jo poori raat mahal ki thandi jheel mein khada rahega, use bada inaam milega.' Ek gareeb aadmi ko parivaar ke liye paison ki zaroorat thi, woh maan gaya, aur subah tak kaanpta hua paani mein khada raha.

text.en: In the morning Akbar asked, 'How did you manage?' 'I looked at a lamp burning far away in the palace window,' the man said. A courtier sneered, 'Then the lamp kept you warm! No reward!' Akbar agreed, and the man left, sad.
text.hinglish: Subah Akbar ne poochha, 'Kaise kar liya?' 'Main door mahal ki khidki mein jalta diya dekhta raha,' aadmi bola. Ek darbaari ne taana maara, 'To diye ne garmi di! Koi inaam nahi!' Akbar maan gaye, aur aadmi udaas hokar chala gaya.

text.en: Birbal said nothing. The next day he didn't come to court. Akbar sent for him. 'I'm cooking khichdi,' came the reply. Hours passed. Finally Akbar went to see for himself.
text.hinglish: Birbal kuch nahi bole. Agle din woh darbaar nahi aaye. Akbar ne bulaawa bheja. 'Khichdi bana raha hoon,' jawaab aaya. Ghante beet gaye. Aakhir Akbar khud dekhne gaye.

text.en: There was Birbal, with a pot of khichdi hanging high up on a tree, and a tiny fire far below on the ground. 'Birbal! How will it ever cook?' 'The same way a faraway lamp warmed a man in the lake, Jahanpanah.'
text.hinglish: Wahan Birbal ne khichdi ki handi ped par bahut oonchi latkaayi thi, aur neeche zameen par chhoti si aag jal rahi thi. 'Birbal! Yeh kaise pakegi?' 'Waise hi Jahanpanah, jaise door ke diye ne jheel mein khade aadmi ko garmi di.'

text.en: Akbar laughed and understood. He called the poor man back and gave him his full reward. Birbal had shown the truth without a harsh word, with a smile and a pot of khichdi.
text.hinglish: Akbar hanse aur samajh gaye. Unhone gareeb aadmi ko wapas bulaakar poora inaam diya. Birbal ne bina kadve shabd ke, muskaan aur khichdi ki handi se sach dikha diya.

say.en: Little one, stand up for what is fair, gently and cleverly.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, jo sahi hai uske liye khade hona, pyaar aur samajh se.

moral.en: Stand up for fairness with kindness and a clever smile.
moral.hinglish: Nyaay ke liye dayaa aur chatur muskaan ke saath khade raho.

reflection.en: When has someone stood up for you kindly?
reflection.hinglish: Kab kisi ne pyaar se aapka saath diya?

q.en: The man stood in the cold lake all night.
q.hinglish: Aadmi poori raat thandi jheel mein khada raha.

q.en: Birbal's khichdi cooked quickly.
q.hinglish: Birbal ki khichdi jaldi pak gayi.

q.en: In the end the poor man got his reward.
q.hinglish: Ant mein gareeb aadmi ko inaam mila.

title.en: How many crows in the city?

text.en: One sunny afternoon, Emperor Akbar was strolling in his garden with Birbal. A crow cawed from the wall, and Akbar had a playful idea. 'Birbal, tell me: how many crows are there in our city?'
text.hinglish: Ek dhoop bhari dopahar Badshah Akbar Birbal ke saath baag mein tahal rahe the. Deewar par ek kauva kaanv-kaanv kar raha tha, aur Akbar ko ek mazedaar khayal aaya. 'Birbal, batao: hamare shehar mein kitne kauve hain?'

text.en: The courtiers smiled. Surely even clever Birbal couldn't count every crow! Birbal stroked his beard, looked at the sky, and thought for just a moment.
text.hinglish: Darbaari muskuraaye. Chatur Birbal bhi har kauva to nahi gin sakte! Birbal ne daadhi sehlaayi, aasmaan dekha, aur bas ek pal socha.

text.en: 'There are ninety-five thousand, four hundred and sixty-three crows in our city, Jahanpanah,' he said confidently. Akbar raised an eyebrow. 'And if we count and find more?'
text.hinglish: 'Hamare shehar mein pachaanve hazaar chaar sau tirsath kauve hain, Jahanpanah,' unhone vishvaas se kaha. Akbar ne bhaunh uthaayi. 'Aur agar ginne par zyada nikle?'

text.en: 'Then some crows have relatives visiting from nearby towns,' said Birbal. 'And if there are fewer?' 'Then some of our crows have gone to visit their relatives!' Akbar burst out laughing, and so did the whole court.
text.hinglish: 'To kuch kauvon ke rishtedaar aas-paas ke shehron se milne aaye honge,' Birbal bole. 'Aur agar kam nikle?' 'To hamare kuch kauve apne rishtedaaron se milne gaye honge!' Akbar zor se hans pade, aur poora darbaar bhi.

text.en: Some questions have no exact answer. A cheerful mind and a sense of humour can turn a tricky moment into a happy one. Laughter is good medicine for everyone, including mothers-to-be!
text.hinglish: Kuch sawaalon ka koi pakka jawaab nahi hota. Khush mann aur thoda mazaak ek mushkil pal ko khushi bhara bana sakta hai. Hansi sabke liye achhi dawa hai, maa banne wali ke liye bhi!

say.en: Little one, I can't wait to hear your first laugh.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tumhari pehli hansi sunne ka intezaar hai.

moral.en: A cheerful, quick mind turns tricky moments into laughter.
moral.hinglish: Khush aur tez dimaag mushkil pal ko hansi mein badal deta hai.

reflection.en: What always makes you laugh? Share it with baby!
reflection.hinglish: Aapko hamesha kis baat par hansi aati hai? Baby ko bataaiye!

q.en: Akbar asked Birbal to count the crows.
q.hinglish: Akbar ne Birbal se kauve ginne ko kaha.

q.en: Birbal counted every crow one by one.
q.hinglish: Birbal ne har kauva ek-ek karke gina.

q.en: Birbal's answer made the court laugh.
q.hinglish: Birbal ke jawaab se darbaar hans pada.

text.en: One hot summer, Tenali Rama's garden was dry, and drawing water from the deep well was hard work. One night he noticed two thieves hiding in the bushes, waiting for the family to sleep.
text.hinglish: Ek tapti garmi mein Tenali Raman ka baag sookh raha tha, aur gehre kuein se paani nikaalna bahut mehnat ka kaam tha. Ek raat unhone dekha ki do chor jhaadiyon mein chhupe hain, parivaar ke sone ka intezaar kar rahe hain.

text.en: Tenali smiled to himself. He said loudly to his wife, 'There are many thieves about. Let's put our jewels and silver in the trunk and drop it into the well. No one will find it there!'
text.hinglish: Tenali man hi man muskuraaye. Unhone patni se zor se kaha, 'Aajkal bahut chor ghoom rahe hain. Chalo gehne aur chaandi sandook mein rakhkar kuein mein daal dete hain. Wahan koi nahi dhoondh paayega!'

text.en: They filled an old trunk with stones and dropped it into the well with a big SPLASH, then went inside to sleep. The thieves rubbed their hands. 'Let's pull out the water and get the treasure!'
text.hinglish: Unhone ek purane sandook mein pathar bhare aur bade 'chhapaak' ke saath kuein mein daal diya, phir sone chale gaye. Chor haath malne lage. 'Chalo paani nikaal kar khazaana nikaalte hain!'

text.en: All night long the thieves pulled up bucket after bucket and poured the water out, right onto Tenali's thirsty garden. By dawn the well was low, they had found only stones, and the garden was soaked and green!
text.hinglish: Poori raat chor baalti par baalti nikaal kar paani phenkte rahe, seedha Tenali ke pyaase baag mein. Subah tak kuan khaali hone laga, unhe sirf pathar mile, aur baag bheeg kar hara ho gaya!

text.en: Tenali came out and thanked them warmly for watering his garden. The embarrassed thieves ran off and never came back. A clever idea turned a problem into a gift.
text.hinglish: Tenali bahar aaye aur baag seenchne ke liye unka dil se shukriya kiya. Sharminda chor bhaag gaye aur kabhi nahi laute. Ek chatur soch ne mushkil ko tohfe mein badal diya.

say.en: Little one, a clever idea can turn trouble into a gift.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, ek chatur idea mushkil ko tohfa bana sakta hai.

moral.en: Quick thinking can turn a problem into an opportunity.
moral.hinglish: Tez soch mushkil ko mauke mein badal sakti hai.

reflection.en: When did a problem in your life turn into something good?
reflection.hinglish: Aapke jeevan ki koi mushkil kab achhi cheez ban gayi?

q.en: Tenali put stones in the trunk.
q.hinglish: Tenali ne sandook mein pathar daale.

q.en: The thieves found real jewels.
q.hinglish: Choron ko asli gehne mile.

q.en: The thieves watered Tenali's garden.
q.hinglish: Choron ne Tenali ka baag seencha.

text.en: A kind Brahmin was given a fine goat as a gift. Happily he put it on his shoulders and set off home through the forest. Three tricksters saw him and made a plan to take the goat.
text.hinglish: Ek bhale Brahman ko daan mein ek sundar bakri mili. Khushi se use kandhe par rakhkar woh jungle ke raaste ghar chal pada. Teen thagon ne use dekha aur bakri lene ki yojana banaayi.

text.en: The first trickster met him on the path. 'Panditji, why are you carrying a dog on your shoulders?' 'It's a goat!' said the Brahmin, and walked on, a little puzzled.
text.hinglish: Pehla thag raaste mein mila. 'Panditji, aap kandhe par kutta kyon le ja rahe hain?' 'Yeh bakri hai!' Brahman bole, aur thoda uljhe hue aage badhe.

text.en: Further on, the second trickster said, 'Panditji, what a strange thing, carrying a dead calf!' Then the third laughed, 'Why carry a donkey, Panditji?' The Brahmin began to doubt his own eyes.
text.hinglish: Aage doosra thag bola, 'Panditji, mara hua bachhda kyon uthaaye hain?' Phir teesra hansa, 'Gadha kyon le ja rahe ho, Panditji?' Brahman apni hi aankhon par shak karne lage.

question.en: Three people say the goat is something else. What should the Brahmin do?
question.hinglish: Teen log kehte hain bakri kuch aur hai. Brahman ko kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Trust what he knows is true
label.hinglish: Jo sach jaante hain us par bharosa karein

lesson.en: Yes! Many voices don't change the truth.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Kai awaazein sach nahi badal deti.

label.en: Stop, look carefully and check
label.hinglish: Rukein, dhyaan se dekhein aur jaanchein

lesson.en: Wise! A calm second look would have shown it was a goat.
lesson.hinglish: Samajhdaari! Dhyaan se dekhne par bakri hi dikhti.

text.en: Confused and worried, he put the goat down and hurried away. The tricksters laughed and took it. Only later did the Brahmin realise he had been fooled by voices, not by facts.
text.hinglish: Uljhan aur ghabraahat mein unhone bakri neeche rakhi aur jaldi se chale gaye. Thag hanse aur bakri le gaye. Baad mein Brahman ko samajh aaya ki unhe tathyon ne nahi, awaazon ne bewakoof banaaya.

text.en: This Panchatantra tale reminds us: don't believe something just because many people say it. Look for yourself, think calmly, and trust what is true.
text.hinglish: Yeh Panchatantra ki kahani yaad dilaati hai: kisi baat ko sirf isliye mat maano kyonki kai log keh rahe hain. Khud dekho, shaanti se socho, aur sach par bharosa rakho.

say.en: Little one, trust your own eyes and a calm mind.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, apni aankhon aur shaant mann par bharosa rakhna.

moral.en: Don't let many voices make you doubt the truth; check for yourself.
moral.hinglish: Kai awaazon se sach par shak mat karo; khud jaancho.

reflection.en: Is there advice you hear often that you've chosen to check for yourself?
reflection.hinglish: Kya koi salaah hai jo aap aksar sunti hain aur khud jaanchna chahti hain?

q.en: The Brahmin was carrying a goat.
q.hinglish: Brahman bakri le ja rahe the.

q.en: It really was a dog.
q.hinglish: Woh sach mein kutta tha.

q.en: Three tricksters fooled him.
q.hinglish: Teen thagon ne unhe bewakoof banaaya.

text.en: Long ago, in a forest near Varanasi, lived a golden deer king called the Banyan Deer. He led his herd with love. The king of Varanasi loved to hunt, and the deer lived in fear.
text.hinglish: Bahut pehle, Varanasi ke paas ke jungle mein, ek sunehra hiran-raja rehta tha jise Bargad Mrig kehte the. Woh pyaar se apne jhund ki agvaayi karta tha. Varanasi ke raja ko shikaar pasand tha, aur hiran dar mein jeete the.

text.en: To stop many deer being hurt in the chase, the Banyan Deer made an agreement with the king: one deer would come each day, by turn, so the rest could live in peace. It was a hard, sad promise.
text.hinglish: Taaki shikaar ki daud mein bahut hiran ghaayal na hon, Bargad Mrig ne raja se samjhauta kiya: baari-baari roz ek hiran jaayega, taaki baaki shaanti se jee sakein. Yeh ek kathin, dukh bhara vaada tha.

text.en: One day it was the turn of a doe who was expecting a baby. She came to the deer king with tears. 'My little one is not born yet. Please, can someone take my turn until my baby arrives?'
text.hinglish: Ek din ek hirni ki baari aayi jo maa banne wali thi. Woh aansuon ke saath hiran-raja ke paas aayi. 'Mera bachcha abhi paida nahi hua. Kripya koi meri baari le le jab tak mera bachcha aa jaaye?'

text.en: The Banyan Deer said gently, 'Go home and rest. I will take your place.' He walked to the palace himself. The king was astonished. 'Why have you come, O king of deer?' He listened to the story, and his eyes filled with tears.
text.hinglish: Bargad Mrig ne pyaar se kaha, 'Ghar jaakar aaraam karo. Tumhari jagah main jaaoonga.' Woh khud mahal gaye. Raja hairaan the. 'Hiranon ke raja, aap kyon aaye?' Unhone kahani suni, aur unki aankhein bhar aayi.

text.en: 'You have taught me what true kindness is,' said the king. He set the Banyan Deer free, promised never to hunt deer again, and protected all the animals of the forest. The doe's baby was born safe in a peaceful forest.
text.hinglish: 'Aapne mujhe sachchi dayaa sikhaayi,' raja ne kaha. Unhone Bargad Mrig ko mukt kiya, kabhi hiran ka shikaar na karne ka vaada kiya, aur jungle ke saare jaanwaron ki raksha ki. Hirni ka bachcha ek shaant jungle mein surakshit paida hua.

say.en: Little one, so many people are already protecting you with love.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, itne log pyaar se abhi se tumhari raksha kar rahe hain.

moral.en: Kindness and care for a mother and child can change even a king's heart.
moral.hinglish: Maa aur bachche ke prati dayaa raja ka dil bhi badal sakti hai.

reflection.en: Who is taking special care of you during this pregnancy?
reflection.hinglish: Is samay kaun aapka khaas khayal rakh raha hai?

q.en: The doe was expecting a baby.
q.hinglish: Hirni maa banne wali thi.

q.en: The Banyan Deer refused to help.
q.hinglish: Bargad Mrig ne madad se mana kiya.

q.en: The king stopped hunting deer.
q.hinglish: Raja ne hiran ka shikaar band kiya.

title.hinglish: Dada ji ka aam ka ped

text.en: In a village in Haryana, an old Dada ji was digging a small hole by the edge of his field. A young traveller stopped. 'Baba, what are you planting?' 'A mango seed,' Dada ji smiled.
text.hinglish: Haryana ke ek gaon mein ek boodhe Dada ji khet ki mend par chhota gaddha khod rahe the. Ek yuva musaafir ruka. 'Baba, kya laga rahe ho?' 'Aam ki guthli,' Dada ji muskuraaye.

text.en: The traveller laughed kindly. 'But a mango tree takes many years to give fruit. You may not get to eat its mangoes, Baba!' Dada ji kept patting the soil with his wrinkled hands.
text.hinglish: Musaafir pyaar se hansa. 'Par aam ke ped par phal aane mein kai saal lagte hain. Shayad aap iske aam na kha paao, Baba!' Dada ji apne jhurridaar haathon se mitti thapthapaate rahe.

text.en: 'When I was a little boy,' he said, 'I ate sweet mangoes from trees that my grandfather planted. He never asked if he would eat them. Now it is my turn to plant for the children who will come.'
text.hinglish: 'Jab main chhota tha,' woh bole, 'maine us ped ke meethe aam khaaye jo mere dada ji ne lagaaya tha. Unhone kabhi nahi poochha ki woh khaayenge ya nahi. Ab meri baari hai aane wale bachchon ke liye lagaane ki.'

text.en: Every morning Dada ji watered the little seedling and told it stories. Years passed. The seedling grew into a strong, shady tree, and one summer it was heavy with golden mangoes.
text.hinglish: Har subah Dada ji nanhe paudhe ko paani dete aur use kahaniyan sunaate. Saal beete. Paudha ek majboot, chhaayadaar ped ban gaya, aur ek garmi mein sunehre aamon se lad gaya.

text.en: Children climbed its branches and swung from its arms. Mothers rested in its shade. Like Dada ji, every family plants love today for children they are still waiting to meet, just as you are doing now.
text.hinglish: Bachche uski daalon par chadhte aur jhoolte. Maayein uski chhaanv mein aaraam karti. Dada ji ki tarah, har parivaar aaj un bachchon ke liye pyaar boota hai jinse milne ka intezaar hai, jaise aap abhi kar rahi hain.

say.en: Little one, we are planting love today, so you can sit in its shade tomorrow.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, hum aaj pyaar bo rahe hain, taaki tum kal uski chhaanv mein baitho.

moral.en: What we lovingly plant today becomes shade for the next generation.
moral.hinglish: Jo aaj pyaar se boate hain, woh agli peedhi ki chhaanv banta hai.

reflection.en: What 'tree' would you like to plant for your child's future?
reflection.hinglish: Aap bachche ke bhavishya ke liye kaun sa 'ped' lagaana chahengi?

q.en: Dada ji planted a mango seed.
q.hinglish: Dada ji ne aam ki guthli lagaayi.

q.en: Dada ji only planted trees for himself.
q.hinglish: Dada ji sirf apne liye ped lagaate the.

q.en: The tree later gave shade to children.
q.hinglish: Ped ne baad mein bachchon ko chhaanv di.

title.en: APJ Abdul Kalam: the boy who watched birds
title.hinglish: APJ Abdul Kalam: chidiyan dekhne wala ladka

text.en: In Rameswaram, a small temple town by the sea in Tamil Nadu, a boy named Abdul Kalam was born in 1931. His father owned boats, and the family lived simply. Young Kalam even sold newspapers to help at home.
text.hinglish: Tamil Nadu ke samudra kinaare chhote mandir-shehar Rameswaram mein 1931 mein Abdul Kalam naam ka ladka paida hua. Pita ki naavein thi, aur parivaar saadgi se rehta tha. Nanhe Kalam ghar ki madad ke liye akhbaar bhi bechte the.

text.en: One day his teacher took the class to the beach and showed them seagulls flying. He explained how birds fly. Kalam watched, amazed. That day a dream took flight in his heart: he wanted to understand flight.
text.hinglish: Ek din unke shikshak class ko samudra kinaare le gaye aur udte samudri pakshi dikhaaye. Unhone samjhaaya ki pakshi kaise udte hain. Kalam hairaani se dekhte rahe. Us din unke dil mein ek sapna uda: udaan ko samajhna.

text.en: He studied hard, often by lamplight, and learned aeronautical engineering at the Madras Institute of Technology. Later, at ISRO, he led the team that launched India's SLV-3 rocket in 1980, placing the Rohini satellite in orbit.
text.hinglish: Unhone mehnat se padhai ki, aksar diye ki roshni mein, aur Madras Institute of Technology se aeronautical engineering seekhi. Baad mein ISRO mein unhone woh team chalaayi jisne 1980 mein Bharat ka SLV-3 rocket chhoda aur Rohini satellite kaksha mein pahunchaaya.

text.en: People lovingly called him the 'Missile Man of India'. In 2002 he became the President of India, and was called the 'People's President' because he was so humble. He still wrote back to children's letters.
text.hinglish: Log unhe pyaar se 'Bharat ka Missile Man' kehte the. 2002 mein woh Bharat ke Rashtrapati bane, aur itne vinamra the ki unhe 'Janta ke Rashtrapati' kaha gaya. Woh bachchon ki chitthiyon ka jawaab tak dete the.

text.en: Dr Kalam loved meeting students and told them, 'Dream, dream, dream. Dreams become thoughts, and thoughts become actions.' A boy who watched birds from a beach taught a whole country to fly.
text.hinglish: Dr Kalam ko vidyarthiyon se milna bahut pasand tha aur woh kehte, 'Sapne dekho, sapne dekho. Sapne vichaar bante hain, aur vichaar karm.' Samudra kinaare chidiyan dekhne wale ladke ne poore desh ko udna sikhaaya.

say.en: Little one, dream big. Your dreams will have wings.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, bade sapne dekhna. Tumhare sapnon ko pankh milenge.

moral.en: Simple beginnings, hard work and big dreams can lift a whole nation.
moral.hinglish: Saada shuruaat, mehnat aur bade sapne poore desh ko upar utha sakte hain.

reflection.en: What dream would you whisper to your baby today?
reflection.hinglish: Aaj aap baby ko kaun sa sapna fusfusaayengi?

q.en: Kalam was born in Rameswaram.
q.hinglish: Kalam Rameswaram mein paida hue.

q.en: Kalam never became President.
q.hinglish: Kalam kabhi Rashtrapati nahi bane.

q.en: Watching birds inspired his dream of flight.
q.hinglish: Chidiyan dekhkar udaan ka sapna jaaga.

title.en: Savitribai Phule, India's first woman teacher
title.hinglish: Savitribai Phule, Bharat ki pehli mahila shikshika

text.en: Savitribai was born in 1831 in Naigaon, Maharashtra. In those days most girls were not allowed to go to school. When she married Jyotirao Phule, he saw how eager she was to learn and taught her to read and write at home.
text.hinglish: Savitribai 1831 mein Maharashtra ke Naigaon mein paida hui. Us zamaane mein zyaadatar ladkiyon ko school jaane nahi diya jaata tha. Jyotirao Phule se vivaah ke baad unhone dekha ki woh seekhne ko kitni utsuk hain, aur ghar par unhe padhna-likhna sikhaaya.

text.en: Savitribai trained as a teacher. In 1848, together with Jyotirao, she opened a school for girls in Pune. She became one of India's first women teachers, helping girls from every community learn.
text.hinglish: Savitribai ne shikshika banne ki training li. 1848 mein Jyotirao ke saath unhone Pune mein ladkiyon ka school khola. Woh Bharat ki pehli mahila shikshikaon mein se ek bani, aur har samaaj ki ladkiyon ko padhaaya.

text.en: Not everyone liked it. On her way to school, some people threw mud and stones at her. So Savitribai carried an extra sari in her bag. At school she changed, smiled, and taught her girls as if nothing had happened.
text.hinglish: Sabko yeh pasand nahi tha. School jaate samay kuch log un par keechad aur pathar phenkte. Isliye Savitribai bag mein ek extra saadi rakhti. School mein kapde badalti, muskuraati, aur ladkiyon ko aise padhaati jaise kuch hua hi na ho.

question.en: People throw mud at Savitribai. What gives her strength?
question.hinglish: Log Savitribai par keechad phenkte hain. Unhe shakti kahan se milti hai?

label.en: Her belief that every girl deserves to learn
label.hinglish: Unka vishvaas ki har ladki ko padhne ka haq hai

lesson.en: Yes! A purpose bigger than yourself makes you brave.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Apne se bada uddeshya insaan ko bahadur banata hai.

label.en: Her husband's support beside her
label.hinglish: Pati ka saath

lesson.en: Right! Jyotirao stood by her; family support is a superpower.
lesson.hinglish: Sahi! Jyotirao unke saath khade rahe; parivaar ka saath super-shakti hai.

text.en: She also wrote beautiful poems, cared for the sick and supported women who needed help. Over the years she and Jyotirao opened many schools.
text.hinglish: Unhone sundar kavitaayein bhi likhi, beemaaron ki seva ki aur zaroorat-mand mahilaon ka saath diya. Saalon mein unhone aur Jyotirao ne kai school khole.

text.en: Today, every girl who opens a schoolbook walks a little on the path Savitribai made. She shows that patience, courage and kindness can change a whole country.
text.hinglish: Aaj har ladki jo school ki kitaab kholti hai, Savitribai ke banaaye raaste par thoda chalti hai. Woh dikhaati hain ki dheeraj, himmat aur dayaa poora desh badal sakti hai.

say.en: Little one, learning is your right and your joy. We will always support you.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, padhna tumhara haq aur tumhari khushi hai. Hum hamesha tumhara saath denge.

moral.en: Courage and patience in teaching others can change a nation.
moral.hinglish: Doosron ko sikhaane ki himmat aur dheeraj desh badal sakte hain.

reflection.en: What would you love your child to learn first from you?
reflection.hinglish: Aap chahengi bachcha sabse pehle aapse kya seekhe?

q.en: Savitribai opened a girls' school in Pune in 1848.
q.hinglish: Savitribai ne 1848 mein Pune mein ladkiyon ka school khola.

q.en: Savitribai stopped teaching when people threw mud.
q.hinglish: Keechad phenkne par Savitribai ne padhaana chhod diya.

q.en: She carried an extra sari to school.
q.hinglish: Woh school ke liye extra saadi le jaati thi.

title.en: Neeraj Chopra: the golden javelin of Panipat
title.hinglish: Neeraj Chopra: Panipat ka sunehra bhaala

text.en: In Khandra village near Panipat, here in Haryana, lived a cheerful, chubby boy named Neeraj. He loved milk, ghee and his family's love! His uncle took him to the gym in Panipat so he could get fit and strong.
text.hinglish: Haryana mein Panipat ke paas Khandra gaon mein Neeraj naam ka ek khushmizaaj, gol-matol ladka rehta tha. Use doodh, ghee aur parivaar ka pyaar bahut pasand tha! Uske chacha use fit aur majboot banaane ke liye Panipat ke gym le gaye.

text.en: At Shivaji Stadium in Panipat he saw older athletes throwing a javelin. He picked one up, threw it, and it flew far. A senior athlete noticed and said, 'You have a talent. Keep practising!'
text.hinglish: Panipat ke Shivaji Stadium mein usne bade khiladiyon ko bhaala phenkte dekha. Usne ek uthaaya, phenka, aur woh door tak gaya. Ek senior khiladi ne dekha aur kaha, 'Tumme hunar hai. Abhyaas karte raho!'

text.en: Neeraj trained day after day, in heat and cold, through injuries and setbacks. He kept a calm mind, a big smile, and a simple rule: do your best on every throw.
text.hinglish: Neeraj ne roz abhyaas kiya, garmi aur sardi mein, chot aur mushkilon ke beech bhi. Usne mann shaant rakha, chehre par muskaan, aur ek seedha niyam: har throw mein apna best do.

question.en: Neeraj gets injured before a big competition. What helps him most?
question.hinglish: Bade muqable se pehle Neeraj ko chot lagti hai. Use sabse zyada kya madad karega?

label.en: Rest, heal patiently and train again
label.hinglish: Aaraam, dheeraj se theek hona, phir abhyaas

lesson.en: Yes! Rest is part of becoming strong.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Aaraam bhi majboot banne ka hissa hai.

label.en: Stay positive and keep his goal in mind
label.hinglish: Sakaaratmak rehna aur lakshya yaad rakhna

lesson.en: Right! A happy, steady mind brings you back stronger.
lesson.hinglish: Sahi! Khush, sthir mann aapko aur majboot lautaata hai.

text.en: At the Tokyo Olympics, on 7 August 2021, Neeraj threw his javelin 87.58 metres and won the gold medal: India's first ever Olympic gold in athletics! The whole country cheered.
text.hinglish: Tokyo Olympics mein, 7 August 2021 ko, Neeraj ne 87.58 metre bhaala phenka aur gold medal jeeta: athletics mein Bharat ka pehla Olympic gold! Poora desh khushi se jhoom utha.

text.en: Back in Khandra, the village celebrated with dhol, laddoos and tears of joy. Neeraj thanked his family, his coaches and his country. A boy from a Haryana village showed that big dreams can grow in small fields.
text.hinglish: Khandra mein gaon ne dhol, laddoo aur khushi ke aansuon se jashn manaaya. Neeraj ne parivaar, coach aur desh ka shukriya kiya. Haryana ke ek gaon ke ladke ne dikhaaya ki bade sapne chhote kheton mein bhi ugte hain.

say.en: Little one, from our home you can throw your dreams as far as the sky.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, hamare ghar se tum apne sapne aasmaan tak phenk sakte ho.

moral.en: Steady practice, a calm mind and family love can take you to gold.
moral.hinglish: Lagaataar abhyaas, shaant mann aur parivaar ka pyaar gold tak le ja sakte hain.

reflection.en: What would you cheer the loudest for in your child's life?
reflection.hinglish: Aap bachche ke jeevan mein kis baat par sabse zor se taali bajaayengi?

q.en: Neeraj Chopra is from a village near Panipat.
q.hinglish: Neeraj Chopra Panipat ke paas ke gaon se hain.

q.en: He won gold at the Tokyo Olympics.
q.hinglish: Unhone Tokyo Olympics mein gold jeeta.

q.en: Neeraj threw a hammer, not a javelin.
q.hinglish: Neeraj ne bhaala nahi, hathauda phenka.

title.en: Mary Kom: a mother and a champion
title.hinglish: Mary Kom: maa bhi, champion bhi

text.en: Mary Kom was born in a small village in Manipur to a family of farmers. As a girl she helped in the fields, cared for her younger siblings and loved every kind of sport.
text.hinglish: Mary Kom Manipur ke ek chhote gaon mein kisaan parivaar mein paida hui. Bachpan mein woh kheton mein madad karti, chhote bhai-behenon ka dhyaan rakhti aur har khel se pyaar karti.

text.en: When she saw boxer Dingko Singh from Manipur win gold at the 1998 Asian Games, she was inspired. She started boxing training, even though some people said boxing was not for girls.
text.hinglish: Jab usne Manipur ke boxer Dingko Singh ko 1998 Asian Games mein gold jeette dekha, to use prerna mili. Usne boxing ki training shuru ki, jabki kuch log kehte the boxing ladkiyon ke liye nahi.

text.en: Mary trained with great discipline and became a world champion. Then she married and became the mother of twin boys. Many thought her boxing days were over.
text.hinglish: Mary ne bahut anushaasan se abhyaas kiya aur world champion bani. Phir unki shaadi hui aur woh judwa beton ki maa bani. Kai logon ne socha ab boxing khatam.

text.en: But Mary came back! With her family's support she trained again and won more world titles after becoming a mother, six world titles in all. At the 2012 London Olympics she won a bronze medal for India.
text.hinglish: Par Mary wapas aayi! Parivaar ke saath se usne phir abhyaas kiya aur maa banne ke baad bhi aur world title jeete, kul chhah world title. 2012 London Olympics mein usne Bharat ke liye bronze medal jeeta.

text.en: Mary Kom shows that being a mother is a strength, not an ending. Love for your children can give you courage you never knew you had.
text.hinglish: Mary Kom dikhaati hain ki maa banna ek shakti hai, ant nahi. Bachchon ka pyaar aisi himmat de sakta hai jo aapko pata bhi nahi thi.

say.en: Little one, becoming your mother is making me stronger every day.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tumhari maa banna mujhe roz aur majboot bana raha hai.

moral.en: Motherhood is a new strength, and dreams can continue after it.
moral.hinglish: Maa banna ek nayi shakti hai, aur sapne uske baad bhi chalte hain.

reflection.en: What dream of your own would you love to keep alive after baby comes?
reflection.hinglish: Baby ke aane ke baad aap apna kaun sa sapna zinda rakhna chahengi?

q.en: Mary Kom is from Manipur.
q.hinglish: Mary Kom Manipur se hain.

q.en: Mary stopped boxing forever after her twins were born.
q.hinglish: Judwa bachchon ke baad Mary ne boxing hamesha ke liye chhod di.

q.en: She won an Olympic bronze in 2012.
q.hinglish: Unhone 2012 mein Olympic bronze jeeta.

title.en: Sakshi Malik: never give up till the last second
title.hinglish: Sakshi Malik: aakhri second tak haar nahi

text.en: In Mokhra village of Rohtak district, Haryana, lived a girl named Sakshi. Her grandfather had been a wrestler, and she loved hearing his stories of the akhada.
text.hinglish: Haryana ke Rohtak zile ke Mokhra gaon mein Sakshi naam ki ladki rehti thi. Uske dada ji pehlwaan the, aur use unki akhaade ki kahaniyan sunna bahut pasand tha.

text.en: At twelve she began training at a wrestling centre in Rohtak. Some neighbours said wrestling was not for girls. Her parents believed in her, and she trained early every morning.
text.hinglish: Baarah saal ki umar mein usne Rohtak ke ek kushti centre mein training shuru ki. Kuch padosiyon ne kaha kushti ladkiyon ke liye nahi. Maata-pita ne us par bharosa kiya, aur woh roz subah-subah abhyaas karti.

text.en: At the 2016 Rio Olympics, Sakshi reached the bronze medal match. Her opponent was strong, and soon Sakshi was behind, 0 to 5. Many people watching thought it was over.
text.hinglish: 2016 Rio Olympics mein Sakshi bronze medal ke muqable tak pahunchi. Saamne wali pehlwaan majboot thi, aur jaldi Sakshi 0-5 se peeche ho gayi. Dekhne wale bahut log soch rahe the ki ab khatam.

question.en: Sakshi is behind 0–5. What should she do?
question.hinglish: Sakshi 0-5 se peeche hai. Use kya karna chahiye?

label.en: Keep fighting calmly till the last second
label.hinglish: Aakhri second tak shaanti se ladti rahe

lesson.en: Yes! That's exactly what she did, and it changed everything.
lesson.hinglish: Haan! Usne bilkul yahi kiya, aur sab badal gaya.

label.en: Remember all her years of practice
label.hinglish: Apne saalon ke abhyaas ko yaad kare

lesson.en: Right! Practice gives you strength exactly when you need it.
lesson.hinglish: Sahi! Abhyaas theek zaroorat ke samay shakti deta hai.

text.en: Sakshi did not give up. She stayed calm, attacked bravely, and in the last moments she scored again and again to win 8–5! She became the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal.
text.hinglish: Sakshi ne haar nahi maani. Woh shaant rahi, himmat se daav lagaaye, aur aakhri palon mein baar-baar ank lekar 8-5 se jeet gayi! Woh Olympic medal jeetne wali pehli Bhartiya mahila pehlwaan bani.

text.en: Mokhra and all of Haryana danced with joy. Sakshi's story tells every child: when things look hard, don't stop. Keep going, keep believing, right to the very end.
text.hinglish: Mokhra aur poora Haryana khushi se naach utha. Sakshi ki kahani har bachche se kehti hai: jab mushkil lage, ruko mat. Chalte raho, vishvaas rakho, bilkul ant tak.

say.en: Little one, never give up. We believe in you till the very end.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, kabhi haar mat maanna. Hum ant tak tum par vishvaas rakhenge.

moral.en: Never give up; things can change in the very last moments.
moral.hinglish: Kabhi haar mat maano; aakhri palon mein bhi sab badal sakta hai.

reflection.en: When did you keep going even though it seemed too late?
reflection.hinglish: Kab aapne der lagne par bhi koshish jaari rakhi?

q.en: Sakshi Malik is from Rohtak district.
q.hinglish: Sakshi Malik Rohtak zile se hain.

q.en: Sakshi gave up when she was behind 0–5.
q.hinglish: 0-5 se peeche hone par Sakshi ne haar maan li.

q.en: She won bronze at the 2016 Rio Olympics.
q.hinglish: Unhone 2016 Rio Olympics mein bronze jeeta.

title.en: Sardar Patel, who joined India together
title.hinglish: Sardar Patel, jinhone Bharat ko joda

text.en: Vallabhbhai Patel was born in 1875 in Gujarat, into a family of farmers. He grew up working in the fields and learned that farmers are the strength of the country.
text.hinglish: Vallabhbhai Patel ka janm 1875 mein Gujarat mein ek kisaan parivaar mein hua. Woh kheton mein kaam karte hue bade hue aur seekha ki kisaan desh ki shakti hain.

text.en: He dreamed of becoming a lawyer. He saved money carefully for years, went to England to study law, and worked so hard that he finished at the top of his class.
text.hinglish: Unka sapna wakeel banne ka tha. Unhone saalon dhyaan se paise bachaaye, kaanoon padhne England gaye, aur itni mehnat ki ki class mein sabse aage rahe.

text.en: Back in India he joined the freedom struggle. In 1928 he led the farmers of Bardoli peacefully when they were unfairly taxed. The farmers won, and the women of Bardoli lovingly gave him a new title: 'Sardar', the leader.
text.hinglish: Bharat lautkar woh aazaadi ki ladaai mein jude. 1928 mein unhone Bardoli ke kisaanon ki shaantipoorn agvaayi ki jab un par anuchit lagaan laga. Kisaan jeete, aur Bardoli ki mahilaon ne pyaar se unhe naya naam diya: 'Sardar', yaani neta.

text.en: After 1947, India had more than 560 princely states, like pieces of a big puzzle. With patience, wisdom and firmness, Sardar Patel brought them together into one India. He is called the 'Iron Man of India'.
text.hinglish: 1947 ke baad Bharat mein 560 se zyada riyaasatein thi, jaise ek badi paheli ke tukde. Dheeraj, samajh aur dridhta se Sardar Patel ne unhe jodkar ek Bharat banaaya. Unhe 'Bharat ka Lauh Purush' kehte hain.

text.en: Today the Statue of Unity in Gujarat, the tallest statue in the world, honours him, and his birthday, 31 October, is celebrated as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, National Unity Day. A farmer's son joined a nation.
text.hinglish: Aaj Gujarat mein duniya ki sabse oonchi pratima, Statue of Unity, unke sammaan mein khadi hai, aur unka janmdin, 31 October, Rashtriya Ekta Diwas ke roop mein manaaya jaata hai. Ek kisaan ke bete ne desh joda.

say.en: Little one, may you always bring people together.
say.hinglish: Mere chhote, tum hamesha logon ko jodne wale bano.

moral.en: Patience and firm, fair leadership can bring people together.
moral.hinglish: Dheeraj aur dridh, nyaayi netritva logon ko jod sakta hai.

reflection.en: How does your family stay united through difficult times?
reflection.hinglish: Mushkil samay mein aapka parivaar ek kaise rehta hai?

q.en: Sardar Patel was from a farming family.
q.hinglish: Sardar Patel kisaan parivaar se the.

q.en: He brought the princely states together into one India.
q.hinglish: Unhone riyaasaton ko jodkar ek Bharat banaaya.

q.en: The title 'Sardar' was given to him in England.
q.hinglish: 'Sardar' ki upaadhi unhe England mein mili.
